firstSeen.title: 2025-10-06 Weekly Edit Proposal
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. Note that due to the size of the proposal it will be split into multiple posts. This proposal includes the following edits: Introduce Keel - Updates references from Launch Agent 2 to Keel now that Keel has publicly launched. Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle - Specifies that Amatsu will only prepare the Initial Calculation with respect to Spark for the October Monthly Settlement Cycle. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation - Adds an expected timeline of January 1, 2026 for Stage 2 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital - Clarifies the definition of Genesis Capital for the Genesis Capital Backstop. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper - Defines the Capped SKY Oracle wrapper to prepare for the launch of stUSDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs - Allows Prime Agents to invest directly in Pendle PTs backed by Ethena Exposures and defines the Required Risk Capital for doing so. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets - Implements an Equivalent Loss framework for Real World Assets to reflect the lower risk of these assets due to the possibility of recovery through legal recourse. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate - Increases the Required Risk Capital Percentage for USCC. Add Near Term Logic For Plume - Adds near term risk requirements for Plume to support Grove’s investment into ACRDX. Define The Executive Process - Adds an initial end-to-end process definition for the Sky Executive Process. Introduce Keel Update references to Launch Agent 2 and minor related edits as specified in the linked Pull Request: Forthcoming Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal by aa-lex · Pull Request #65 · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle Add a new subdocument of A.2.5.1.2.1.6 - Interim Measures (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Process Definition - Interim Measures (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.2.5.1.2.1.6.2 - Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Process Definition - Interim Measures - Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Process For October 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (Core) - For the Monthly Settlement Cycle conducted in October 2025, the Initial Calculation prepared by Operational Executor Agent Amatsu will only include calculations related to Spark. The Independent Calculation prepared by BA Labs on behalf of the Core Council will be prepared normally. The calculations related to Spark will be subject to the normal resolution process defined in A.2.6 - Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis . For all other calculations, the amounts in the Independent Calculation will be treated as Agreed Amounts. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation Replace A.2.5.1.2.2.2.2 - Stage 2 Timing (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Implementation Stages - Stage 2 - Stage 2 Timing (GitHub) to read as follows: Stage 2 Timing (Core) - Stage 2 is currently expected to be implemented in the February 2026 Monthly Settlement Cycle for the period from January 1, 2026 to January 31, 2026. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital Replace A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Core) - If a “SKY Backstop Event” is in progress and the SKY price equals zero, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized exactly to restore the Surplus Buffer to zero. Add a new subdocument of A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.8.1.5.5 - Genesis Agents (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Agents to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital (Core) - The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper Add new subdocuments of A.4.4.1.2 - SKY-Backed Borrowing (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.4.4.1.2.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper (Core) - In order to prevent excessive price spikes if there is high demand for leverage against SKY tokens, which could potentially lead to excessive USDS borrowing against SKY, a wrapper for the SKY OSM contract has been developed. The wrapper enforces an upper limit on the price of SKY for the purposes of SKY-Backed Borrowing, which is set to be the minimum value of: The current price reported by PIP_SKY. The cap that has been set on the OSM wrapper contract. A.4.4 - Cap Parameter (Core) - The subdocuments herein further describe the cap parameter and the process for its modification. A.4.4 - Definition (Core) - The cap parameter represents one of the potential inputs for the SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper. The OSM wrapper uses the minimum value of the cap or the PIP_SKY oracle price to determine the price utilized for SKY-backed borrowing. A.4.4 - Modification (Core) - The Core Facilitator, in consultation with BA Labs, has the ability to modify the cap parameter. The modification of said parameter is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll. A.4.4 - Current Value (Core) - The current value of the cap parameter is: 0.04 USDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Core) - Ethena Exposures consist of Direct Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures ), Indirect Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures ), and Pendle Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures). The Instance Financial RRC for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3.1 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Restrictions On Investments On Plume (Core) - Investments on Plume are subject to the following restrictions: Assets other than RWAs on Plume or being bridged to Plume require 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments on Plume may not exceed 125 million USDS.

firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. Note that due to the size of the proposal it will be split into multiple posts. This proposal includes the following edits: Introduce Keel - Updates references from Launch Agent 2 to Keel now that Keel has publicly launched. Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle - Specifies that Amatsu will only prepare the Initial Calculation with respect to Spark for the October Monthly Settlement Cycle. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation - Adds an expected timeline of January 1, 2026 for Stage 2 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital - Clarifies the definition of Genesis Capital for the Genesis Capital Backstop. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper - Defines the Capped SKY Oracle wrapper to prepare for the launch of stUSDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs - Allows Prime Agents to invest directly in Pendle PTs backed by Ethena Exposures and defines the Required Risk Capital for doing so. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets - Implements an Equivalent Loss framework for Real World Assets to reflect the lower risk of these assets due to the possibility of recovery through legal recourse. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate - Increases the Required Risk Capital Percentage for USCC. Add Near Term Logic For Plume - Adds near term risk requirements for Plume to support Grove’s investment into ACRDX. Define The Executive Process - Adds an initial end-to-end process definition for the Sky Executive Process. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital Replace A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Core) - If a “SKY Backstop Event” is in progress and the SKY price equals zero, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized exactly to restore the Surplus Buffer to zero. Add a new subdocument of A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.8.1.5.5 - Genesis Agents (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Agents to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital (Core) - The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper Add new subdocuments of A.4.4.1.2 - SKY-Backed Borrowing (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.4.4.1.2.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper (Core) - In order to prevent excessive price spikes if there is high demand for leverage against SKY tokens, which could potentially lead to excessive USDS borrowing against SKY, a wrapper for the SKY OSM contract has been developed. The wrapper enforces an upper limit on the price of SKY for the purposes of SKY-Backed Borrowing, which is set to be the minimum value of: The current price reported by PIP_SKY. The cap that has been set on the OSM wrapper contract. A.4.4 - Cap Parameter (Core) - The subdocuments herein further describe the cap parameter and the process for its modification. A.4.4 - Definition (Core) - The cap parameter represents one of the potential inputs for the SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper. The OSM wrapper uses the minimum value of the cap or the PIP_SKY oracle price to determine the price utilized for SKY-backed borrowing. A.4.4 - Modification (Core) - The Core Facilitator, in consultation with BA Labs, has the ability to modify the cap parameter. The modification of said parameter is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Core) - Ethena Exposures consist of Direct Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures ), Indirect Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures ), and Pendle Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures). The Instance Financial RRC for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates - Allows Spark delegates to disclose conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation instead of publicly to avoid compromising anonymity. Add pyUSD To Risk Framework - Adds rules for RRC and ASC for investments in pyUSD to the Risk Framework. Move Authority For Approving Additional Lending Markets To The Core Executor Agents - Moves the authority for approving additional lending markets to the Core Executor Agents. Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process - Updates the SparkLend multisig and clarifies the governance process for updates to multisig signers. firstSeen.title: 2025-10-06 Weekly Edit Proposal
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. Note that due to the size of the proposal it will be split into multiple posts. This proposal includes the following edits: Introduce Keel - Updates references from Launch Agent 2 to Keel now that Keel has publicly launched. Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle - Specifies that Amatsu will only prepare the Initial Calculation with respect to Spark for the October Monthly Settlement Cycle. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation - Adds an expected timeline of January 1, 2026 for Stage 2 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital - Clarifies the definition of Genesis Capital for the Genesis Capital Backstop. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper - Defines the Capped SKY Oracle wrapper to prepare for the launch of stUSDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs - Allows Prime Agents to invest directly in Pendle PTs backed by Ethena Exposures and defines the Required Risk Capital for doing so. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets - Implements an Equivalent Loss framework for Real World Assets to reflect the lower risk of these assets due to the possibility of recovery through legal recourse. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate - Increases the Required Risk Capital Percentage for USCC. Add Near Term Logic For Plume - Adds near term risk requirements for Plume to support Grove’s investment into ACRDX. Define The Executive Process - Adds an initial end-to-end process definition for the Sky Executive Process. Introduce Keel Update references to Launch Agent 2 and minor related edits as specified in the linked Pull Request: Forthcoming Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal by aa-lex · Pull Request #65 · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle Add a new subdocument of A.2.5.1.2.1.6 - Interim Measures (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Process Definition - Interim Measures (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.2.5.1.2.1.6.2 - Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Process Definition - Interim Measures - Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Process For October 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (Core) - For the Monthly Settlement Cycle conducted in October 2025, the Initial Calculation prepared by Operational Executor Agent Amatsu will only include calculations related to Spark. The Independent Calculation prepared by BA Labs on behalf of the Core Council will be prepared normally. The calculations related to Spark will be subject to the normal resolution process defined in A.2.6 - Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis . For all other calculations, the amounts in the Independent Calculation will be treated as Agreed Amounts. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation Replace A.2.5.1.2.2.2.2 - Stage 2 Timing (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Implementation Stages - Stage 2 - Stage 2 Timing (GitHub) to read as follows: Stage 2 Timing (Core) - Stage 2 is currently expected to be implemented in the February 2026 Monthly Settlement Cycle for the period from January 1, 2026 to January 31, 2026. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital Replace A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Core) - If a “SKY Backstop Event” is in progress and the SKY price equals zero, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized exactly to restore the Surplus Buffer to zero. Add a new subdocument of A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.8.1.5.5 - Genesis Agents (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Agents to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital (Core) - The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper Add new subdocuments of A.4.4.1.2 - SKY-Backed Borrowing (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.4.4.1.2.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper (Core) - In order to prevent excessive price spikes if there is high demand for leverage against SKY tokens, which could potentially lead to excessive USDS borrowing against SKY, a wrapper for the SKY OSM contract has been developed. The wrapper enforces an upper limit on the price of SKY for the purposes of SKY-Backed Borrowing, which is set to be the minimum value of: The current price reported by PIP_SKY. The cap that has been set on the OSM wrapper contract. A.4.4 - Cap Parameter (Core) - The subdocuments herein further describe the cap parameter and the process for its modification. A.4.4 - Definition (Core) - The cap parameter represents one of the potential inputs for the SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper. The OSM wrapper uses the minimum value of the cap or the PIP_SKY oracle price to determine the price utilized for SKY-backed borrowing. A.4.4 - Modification (Core) - The Core Facilitator, in consultation with BA Labs, has the ability to modify the cap parameter. The modification of said parameter is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll. A.4.4 - Current Value (Core) - The current value of the cap parameter is: 0.04 USDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Core) - Ethena Exposures consist of Direct Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures ), Indirect Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures ), and Pendle Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures). The Instance Financial RRC for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process - Updates the SparkLend multisig and clarifies the governance process for updates to multisig signers. A.3.4 - Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. firstSeen.title: 2025-10-06 Weekly Edit Proposal
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. Note that due to the size of the proposal it will be split into multiple posts. This proposal includes the following edits: Introduce Keel - Updates references from Launch Agent 2 to Keel now that Keel has publicly launched. Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle - Specifies that Amatsu will only prepare the Initial Calculation with respect to Spark for the October Monthly Settlement Cycle. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation - Adds an expected timeline of January 1, 2026 for Stage 2 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital - Clarifies the definition of Genesis Capital for the Genesis Capital Backstop. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper - Defines the Capped SKY Oracle wrapper to prepare for the launch of stUSDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs - Allows Prime Agents to invest directly in Pendle PTs backed by Ethena Exposures and defines the Required Risk Capital for doing so. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets - Implements an Equivalent Loss framework for Real World Assets to reflect the lower risk of these assets due to the possibility of recovery through legal recourse. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate - Increases the Required Risk Capital Percentage for USCC. Add Near Term Logic For Plume - Adds near term risk requirements for Plume to support Grove’s investment into ACRDX. Define The Executive Process - Adds an initial end-to-end process definition for the Sky Executive Process. Introduce Keel Update references to Launch Agent 2 and minor related edits as specified in the linked Pull Request: Forthcoming Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal by aa-lex · Pull Request #65 · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle Add a new subdocument of A.2.5.1.2.1.6 - Interim Measures (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Process Definition - Interim Measures (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.2.5.1.2.1.6.2 - Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Process Definition - Interim Measures - Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Process For October 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (Core) - For the Monthly Settlement Cycle conducted in October 2025, the Initial Calculation prepared by Operational Executor Agent Amatsu will only include calculations related to Spark. The Independent Calculation prepared by BA Labs on behalf of the Core Council will be prepared normally. The calculations related to Spark will be subject to the normal resolution process defined in A.2.6 - Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis . For all other calculations, the amounts in the Independent Calculation will be treated as Agreed Amounts. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation Replace A.2.5.1.2.2.2.2 - Stage 2 Timing (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Implementation Stages - Stage 2 - Stage 2 Timing (GitHub) to read as follows: Stage 2 Timing (Core) - Stage 2 is currently expected to be implemented in the February 2026 Monthly Settlement Cycle for the period from January 1, 2026 to January 31, 2026. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital Replace A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Core) - If a “SKY Backstop Event” is in progress and the SKY price equals zero, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized exactly to restore the Surplus Buffer to zero. Add a new subdocument of A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.8.1.5.5 - Genesis Agents (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Agents to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital (Core) - The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper Add new subdocuments of A.4.4.1.2 - SKY-Backed Borrowing (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.4.4.1.2.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper (Core) - In order to prevent excessive price spikes if there is high demand for leverage against SKY tokens, which could potentially lead to excessive USDS borrowing against SKY, a wrapper for the SKY OSM contract has been developed. The wrapper enforces an upper limit on the price of SKY for the purposes of SKY-Backed Borrowing, which is set to be the minimum value of: The current price reported by PIP_SKY. The cap that has been set on the OSM wrapper contract. A.4.4 - Cap Parameter (Core) - The subdocuments herein further describe the cap parameter and the process for its modification. A.4.4 - Definition (Core) - The cap parameter represents one of the potential inputs for the SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper. The OSM wrapper uses the minimum value of the cap or the PIP_SKY oracle price to determine the price utilized for SKY-backed borrowing. A.4.4 - Modification (Core) - The Core Facilitator, in consultation with BA Labs, has the ability to modify the cap parameter. The modification of said parameter is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll. A.4.4 - Current Value (Core) - The current value of the cap parameter is: 0.04 USDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Core) - Ethena Exposures consist of Direct Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures ), Indirect Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures ), and Pendle Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures). The Instance Financial RRC for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3.1 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Restrictions On Investments On Plume (Core) - Investments on Plume are subject to the following restrictions: Assets other than RWAs on Plume or being bridged to Plume require 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments on Plume may not exceed 125 million USDS.

lastEdit.title: 2025-08-25 Atlas Weekly Cycle Proposal Edits
lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Change Funding Source For Accessibility Reward Wallet - Updates the Accessibility Reward wallet to be funded by Executive Votes rather than the Launch Project. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates - Allows Spark delegates to disclose conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation instead of publicly to avoid compromising anonymity. Add pyUSD To Risk Framework - Adds rules for RRC and ASC for investments in pyUSD to the Risk Framework. Clarify Approval Requirements For Agent Root Edits - Makes minor edits to clarify approval threshold for Agent Root Edits and handling of abstentions. Move Authority For Approving Additional Lending Markets To The Core Executor Agents - Moves the authority for approving additional lending markets to the Core Executor Agents. Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process - Updates the SparkLend multisig and clarifies the governance process for updates to multisig signers. Correct Responsible Party For Updating Active Data - Corrects the Responsible Party for updating some Active Data to be Operational GovOps rather than the Operational Facilitator. Complete Renaming Of “Star” To “Prime” - Replaces remaining references in the Atlas to “Star” with “Prime”. Change Funding Source For Accessibility Reward Wallet Replace A.2.3.8.1.2.1.4.3.1 - Near Term Process (Portal) / A.2.4 - Near Term Process (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Near-Term Process (Core) - In the near term, DAOcraft calculates the Accessibility Reward on behalf of the Support Facilitators. The Accessibility Facilitators then pay the Accessibility Reward from the Accessibility Reward Controller Wallet located on the Ethereum Mainnet at 0x05f471262d15eeca4059dade070e5bed509a4e73 within seven (7) days of the end of every month. The balance of this wallet may be topped up to 3 million USDS. This funding is subject to an Executive Vote. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.3.1.3.3.4 - Abstain Only for Disclosed Conflicts (Portal) / Spark - Abstain Only for Disclosed Conflicts (GitHub) to read as follows: Disclosure Of Conflicts (Core) - Conflicts must be disclosed to the Spark Foundation before the voting window (see Root Edit Token Holder Vote ) for the proposal begins. Abstaining For Non-Disclosed Conflicts (Core) - Abstaining for any reason other than a disclosed conflict is treated as non-performance under Delegate Offboarding . Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.4.2.2 - Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (Portal) / Spark - Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (GitHub) to read as follows: Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (Core) - At onboarding, prospective Delegates must provide any known conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation. Disclosures must be updated as new conflicts arise. Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.8 - Registry of Delegates (Portal) / Spark - Registry of Delegates (GitHub) to read as follows: Registry of Delegates (Core) - The subdocuments herein list each active Delegate’s name, wallet address, effective date, and status. Entries are maintained via an Active Data document updated by the Operational Facilitator. Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.8.1 - Template Information For Each Delegate (Portal) / Spark - Template Information For Each Delegate (GitHub) to read as follows: Template Information For Each Delegate (Core) - The list of Delegates must follow this template for each recorded Delegate: [Insert Delegate Handle] Delegate Name: [Insert Handle] Delegate Wallet Address: Effective Date: Status: Active/Inactive/Suspended Add pyUSD To Risk Framework Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.6.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for Cash Stablecoins, a 0% Instance Financial RRC will be applied to Cash Stablecoins. In the near term, only USDS, sUSDS, Dai, sDai, USDC, USDT, and pyUSD (either held directly or through decentralized exchanges such as Curve) will be eligible for investment under this provision. Add a new subdocument of A.3.4.2.1 - Definitions (Portal) / A.3.4 - Definitions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.4.2.1.2 - Low Risk Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.4 - Low Risk Real World Assets (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Cash Stablecoins (Core) - Cash Stablecoins are defined as USDC, USDT, and pyUSD. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.4.2.2.1 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements. A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC in the LitePSM; USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; Cash Stablecoins in Curve (paired with USDS); USDC in GUNI 0.01%; and USDC in GUNI 0.05%. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral consists of Cash Stablecoins that do not qualify as Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral but can be converted to Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may include Cash Stablecoins deposited into lending protocols, Cash Stablecoins used to provide liquidity to decentralized exchanges, or liquid staking derivatives of cash stablecoins. Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral: The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles; The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: Cash Stablecoins in Curve (not paired with USDS); Cash Stablecoins in Uniswap; Cash Stablecoins in SparkLend; Cash Stablecoins in Aave; Cash Stablecoins in Morpho; and Cash Stablecoins in a Prime ALM Proxy. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may impose limitations on the size of exposures to these protocols or to specific pools within these protocols that qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral in order to prevent excessive risk to Sky. A.3.4 - Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral. firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. Due to the size of this proposal it is split into two posts. Note that this proposal will be updated over the weekend with the address of the Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig. This proposal includes the following edits: Prepare For Deployment Of LayerZero Bridge - Adds initial parameters to prepare for the deployment of the Solana LayerZero bridge, which will replace the existing Wormhole bridge. Update Accessibility Reward Primitive - Renames the Accessibility Reward to Distribution Reward and includes new logic regarding a boosted Distribution Reward. Rename Risk Tolerance Ratio To Encumbrance Ratio - Renames the Risk Tolerance Ratio to Encumbrance Ratio. Add Allocation System Primitive Documents For Launch Agent 4 - Adds documentation for the Allocation System Primitive for Launch Agent 4. Add New Active Instances For Grove - Adds new deployments in the Grove Liquidity Layer. Change Ecosystem Entity Grants To Past Tense - Updates language regarding August 2025 grants to reflect that the transfers have been executed. Clarify Process For Pioneer Chain Reimbursements - Clarifies the process for reimbursements for Pioneer Primes. Update Reference In Risk Framework - Corrects the internal references in two documents in the Risk Framework. Update Language Regarding MKR To SKY Upgrade - Updates the documentation regarding the MKR to SKY upgrade process to reflect that the different stages have been implemented. Prepare For Deployment Of LayerZero Bridge Add new subdocuments of A.1.9.3.2 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.1.9.3.2.13 - Linear Interpolation Module (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.1.9 - Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig (Core) - The Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig (see A.1.9 - Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig) can freeze LayerZero bridges deployed in the Sky Ecosystem without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process. Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the freeze function. A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig (Core) - The Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig (see A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig) can freeze the Solana LayerZero bridge without the need for inclusion in a Spell through the standard Executive Vote process. Each action executed by the multisig, including any function calls and their parameters, must be reported to the Sky community within a reasonable time frame through a post on the Sky Forum. Such actions include activating or disabling the freeze function. Add new subdocuments of A.1.9.4 - Governance Security Culture And Research (Portal) / A.1.9 - A4 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.1.9.4.1 - Spark Agent (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - Spark Agent (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Bridge (Core) - Sky uses a LayerZero bridge to securely move assets between Ethereum Mainnet and Solana, as well as to provide governance controls for Sky-issued tokens on Solana. Additional details regarding the Solana LayerZero Bridge will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas. A.1.9 - Introduction (Core) - The Solana LayerZero Bridge consists of both a Token Bridge that allows bridging USDS between Ethereum Mainnet and Solana as well as a Governance Bridge that allows exercising governance control for Sky-issued tokens on Solana. The Solana LayerZero Bridge replaces the existing Wormhole bridge, which will be deactivated following the first phase of deployment of the LayerZero bridge. The Solana LayerZero bridge serves as the template for future bridges that will be deployed by the Sky Ecosystem across other blockchains. A.1.9 - Deployment (Core) - The Solana LayerZero Bridge will be deployed in two phases. The first phase will occur in the November 13th Executive Vote and the second phase will occur in a subsequent Out-Of-Schedule Executive Vote. The timing and contents of these phases may be modified by the Core Facilitator in consultation with relevant Ecosystem Actors. A.1.9 - Security Parameters (Core) - The documents herein define the security parameters of the Solana LayerZero bridge. A.1.9 - Freezer Multisigs (Core) - The documents herein define two freezer multisigs that have the ability to freeze the Solana LayerZero Bridge from either the Ethereum Mainnet or Solana sides, respectively. A.1.9 - Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig (Core) - The Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig has the ability to freeze the Solana LayerZero Bridge from the Ethereum Mainnet A.1.9 - Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig Address (Core) - The address of the Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig on the Ethereum Mainnet is 0x38d1114b4cE3e079CC0f627df6aC2776B5887776 . A.1.9 - Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig Required Number Of Signers (Core) - The Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig has a 2/4 signing requirement. A.1.9 - Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig Signers (Core) - The signers of the Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig are two (2) addresses controlled by the Core Facilitator and two (2) addresses controlled by Core GovOps. A.1.9 - Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig Usage Standards (Core) - The Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig can only be used in urgent or emergency situations (e.g., potential code exploits). Such situations are characterized by the fact that 1) they have the potential to harm the Sky Ecosystem or its users; and 2) the preparation time required for an Executive Vote would leave the ecosystem vulnerable to harm (e.g., an exploit). The multisig should be used to prevent technical vulnerabilities; prevent unwanted functionality of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system (e.g., price oracles); or prevent unwanted usage of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system which deviates from intended behavior. The Core Council must ensure that use of the multisig is generally aligned and specifically accords with these requirements. A.1.9 - Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig Modification (Core) - The Core Facilitator and Core GovOps can change the signers of the Ethereum LayerZero Freezer Multisig so long as: there are four (4) signers; two (2) signers are required to execute transactions; and an equal number of signers are controlled by the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps. A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig (Core) - The Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas. A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig Address (Core) - The address of the Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig on Solana is 5hARLsT1VA2AmuGL2AXUeSyyFG6o2Fcpb9S6aKXNsbeK . A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig Required Number Of Signers (Core) - The Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig has a 2/4 signing requirement. A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig Signers (Core) - The signers of the Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig are two (2) addresses controlled by Amatsu and two (2) addresses controlled by Keel. A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig Usage Standards (Core) - The Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig can only be used in urgent or emergency situations (e.g., potential code exploits). Such situations are characterized by the fact that 1) they have the potential to harm the Sky Ecosystem or its users; and 2) the preparation time required for an Executive Vote would leave the ecosystem vulnerable to harm (e.g., an exploit). The multisig should be used to prevent technical vulnerabilities; prevent unwanted functionality of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system (e.g., price oracles); or prevent unwanted usage of the smart contracts or corresponding parts of the system which deviates from intended behavior. The Core Council must ensure that use of the multisig is generally aligned and specifically accords with these requirements. A.1.9 - Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig Modification (Core) - Amatsu and Keel can change the signers of the Solana LayerZero Freezer Multisig so long as: there are four (4) signers; two (2) signers are required to execute transactions; and an equal number of signers are controlled by Amatsu and Keel. A.1.9 - Rate Limits (Core) - The documents herein define the rate limits for the Solana LayerZero Bridge. A.1.9 - Rate Limit Accounting (Core) - The Solana LayerZero Bridge uses net accounting. Net accounting means that the rate limit applies to the net amount of tokens transferred from one side of the bridge to the other. For example, if 25,000,000 USDS were transferred from Ethereum Mainnet to Solana and 15,000,000 USDS were transferred from Solana to Ethereum Mainnet, the net amount transferred would be 10,000,000 USDS. A.1.9 - Rate Limit (Core) - The Solana LayerZero Bridge currently has a rate limit of 10,000,000 USDS per day. This limit should be gradually increased over time as the bridge becomes more mature. The rate limit for the Solana LayerZero Bridge may be modified by the Core Facilitator, in consultation with the Core Council Risk Advisor, through the Operational Weekly Cycle. Such modifications can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll. A.1.9 - Validators (Core) - The documents herein specify the selection and configuration of validators for the Solana LayerZero Bridge. A.1.9 - Token Bridge (Core) - The documents herein specify the selection and configuration of validators for the Token Bridge component of the Solana LayerZero Bridge. A.1.9 - Validators (Core) - The validators for the Token Bridge are LayerZero and Nethermind. A.1.9 - Quorum Requirement (Core) - The quorum requirement for the Token Bridge is 2/2. A.1.9 - Governance Bridge (Core) - The documents herein specify the selection and configuration of validators for the Governance Bridge component of the Solana LayerZero Bridge. A.1.9 - Validators (Core) - The validators for the Governance Bridge are LayerZero, Nethermind, Canary, Deutsche Telekom, P2P, Horizon, and Luganodes. A.1.9 - Quorum Requirement (Core) - The quorum requirement for the Token Bridge is 4/7. Update Accessibility Reward Primitive Replace A.2.3.8.1.2.1.3 - Fees (Portal) / A.2.4 - Fees (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.2.4 - Distribution Reward Rate - The standard Distribution Reward rate is set at 0.2%. The Distribution Reward rate is annualized on all USDS and sUSDS balances associated with the relevant Reward Code. A.2.4 - Boosted Distribution Reward Rate - An additional 0.3% Boosted Distribution Reward rate will be available starting January 2026 as specified in the documents herein. This Boosted Distribution Reward may be discontinued in the future at the discretion of Sky Governance. A.2.4 - Approval Process - A Prime Agent may request the Boosted Distribution Reward rate for a specific Instance by posting on the Sky Forum under the “Sky Core” category. The Core Council will review requests and approve them at its discretion. The Core Facilitator must respond to each request with an approval or rejection decision in the thread of the original post. A.2.4 - Specification In The Instance Configuration Document - Prime Agent Instances approved for the Boosted Distribution Reward rate must document this designation in their Instance Configuration Document under “Custom Instance Parameters”. A.2.4 - Limitations - The Boosted Distribution Reward rate is not applicable to USDS and sUSDS balances held by the Prime Agent itself. Call swapUSDSToUSDC Function (Core) - Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDS to USDC via the PSM. To do so, they must call the swapUSDSToUSDC function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the equivalent amount of USDS for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert. The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC) for the PSM. The contract will convert the USDC amount to an 18-decimal format using psmTo18ConversionFactor. The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the converted amount from the ALM Proxy. The contract will swap USDS to Dai at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending Dai to the proxy. The contract will approve the PSM to spend the Dai. The contract will swap Dai to USDC at a 1:1 ratio with no fee via psm.buyGemNoFee, sending USDC to the proxy. The function call is as follows: function swapUSDSToUSDC(uint256 usdcAmount) external Swap USDC To USDS (Core) - The documents herein define a series of operations for an operator to swap USDC to USDS through the PSM. Call swapUSDCToUSDS Function (Core) - Only an operator with the relayer role can swap USDC to USDS via the PSM. To do so, they must call the swapUSDCToUSDS function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the usdcAmount (denominated in 1e6 precision to match PSM USDC handling). The operation will only succeed if the ALM Proxy holds at least the amount of USDC specified for the swap; otherwise, the transaction will revert. The rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting for swaps. Calling this function will carry out the following actions: The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert. The contract will ensure the swap amount is within the allowed rate limit (LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC) for the PSM. The contract will approve the PSM to spend the USDC from the ALM Proxy. The contract will calculate the swap limit per transaction based on the Dai balance held by the PSM, converting with psmTo18ConversionFactor. If the usdcAmount is less than or equal to the limit, the contract will perform a direct swap of USDC to Dai. If the usdcAmount exceeds the limit, the contract will split the swap into multiple smaller swaps: refill the PSM with Dai via psm.fill, recalculate the limit, swap the maximum allowed amount, update the remaining amount, and repeat until complete (reverting with “DssLitePsm/nothing-to-fill” if PSM cannot be filled). The contract will convert the USDC amount to a Dai amount, accounting for token decimal differences. The contract will approve the daiUsds contract to spend the Dai amount from the ALM Proxy. The contract will swap Dai to USDS at a 1:1 ratio via daiUsds, sending USDS to the proxy. The function call is as follows: function swapUSDCToUSDS(uint256 usdcAmount) external Transfer Token Via LayerZero (Core) - The documents herein define the steps for a relayer to transfer a token via LayerZero to a destination endpoint, with the assets sent according to the configured recipient.
