The Rate Limits must be maintained in line with Launch Agent 4’s strategy, market conditions, and security considerations. Get Rate Limit Data (Core) - Anyone can query the full rate limit data for a specific key. Calling this function will carry out the following actions: The contract will return the stored Rate LimitData struct from the _data mapping for the key. The function call is as follows: function getRate LimitData(bytes32 key) external override view returns (Rate LimitData memory) Set Rate Limit Data (Core) - Only an operator with the admin role is able to set or update rate limit data for a specific key, including maxAmount, slope, and historical values. There are two overloads for flexibility. Calling these functions will carry out the following actions: The contract will require that lastAmount is less than or equal to maxAmount, reverting with “Rate Limits/invalid-lastAmount” if not. The contract will require that lastUpdated is less than or equal to the current block timestamp, reverting with “Rate Limits/invalid-lastUpdated” if not. The contract will store the provided data in the _data mapping as a Rate LimitData struct. The contract will emit a Rate LimitDataSet event with the key and provided values. The function calls are as follows: function setRate LimitData(bytes32 key, uint256 maxAmount, uint256 slope, uint256 lastAmount, uint256 lastUpdated) public override onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) function setRate LimitData(bytes32 key, uint256 maxAmount, uint256 slope) external override Set Unlimited Rate Limit Data (Core) - Only an operator with the admin role is able to set unlimited rate limit data for a specific key by configuring it with maximum values. Calling this function will carry out the following actions: The contract will call setRate LimitData internally with type(uint256).max for maxAmount and lastAmount, 0 for slope, and the current block timestamp for lastUpdated. The function call is as follows: function setUnlimitedRate LimitData(bytes32 key) external override Get Current Rate Limit (Core) - Anyone can query the current rate limit value for a specific key, accounting for time-based slope accrual. Calling this function will carry out the following actions: The contract will retrieve the Rate LimitData for the key from the _data mapping. If maxAmount is type(uint256).max (unlimited case), the contract will return type(uint256).max. Otherwise, the contract will calculate and return the minimum of (slope * time elapsed since lastUpdated + lastAmount) and maxAmount. The function call is as follows: function getCurrentRate Limit(bytes32 key) public override view returns (uint256) Trigger Rate Limit Decrease (Core) - Only an operator with the controller role can trigger a decrease in the rate limit for a specific key by a given amount. Calling this function will carry out the following actions: The contract will retrieve the Rate LimitData storage for the key from the data mapping. The contract will require that maxAmount is greater than 0, reverting with “Rate Limits/zero-maxAmount” if not. If maxAmount is type(uint256).max (unlimited case), the contract will return type(uint256).max without changes. The contract will calculate the currentRate Limit using getCurrentRate Limit. The contract will require that amountToDecrease is less than or equal to currentRate Limit, reverting with “Rate Limits/rate-limit-exceeded” if not. The contract will update lastAmount to currentRate Limit minus amountToDecrease and set lastUpdated to the current block timestamp. The contract will emit a Rate LimitDecreaseTriggered event with the key, amountToDecrease, currentRate Limit, and newLimit. The contract will return the newLimit. The function call is as follows: function removeRelayer(address relayer) external Redeem All Mainnet Positions (Core) - The documents herein define the actions that should be performed by an operator if there is a need to recover the liquidity from Mainnet Protocols and centralize it in the Mainnet Launch Agent 4 ALM Proxy. ERC-4626 Withdrawal Action (Core) - In order to withdraw all ERC-4626 balances, the operator must call the redeemERC4626 function. The function call is as follows: function redeemERC4626(address(token), token.balanceOf(address(proxy))) For more detailed instructions on the code to execute this, see ERC-4626 Functions. USDC To USDS Swap Action (Core) - This document defines the action that should be performed by an operator if there is a need to centralize all recovered liquidity in USDS. The operator must call the swapUSDCToUSDS function. The function call is as follows: function swapUSDCToUSDS(usdc.balanceOf(address(proxy)) For more detailed instructions on the code to execute this see Swap USDC To USDS. USDS Burn Action (Core) - This document defines the action that should be performed if there is a need to repay and then burn Launch Agent 4’s USDS debt. The operator must call the burnUSDS function. The function call is as follows: function burnUSDS(usds.balanceOf(address(proxy)) More detailed instructions on the code to execute this, see Burn USDS. Allocation Strategy (Core) - In the future, additional logic will be added herein regarding the strategy by which capital is allocated between different Instances of the Launch Agent 4 Liquidity Layer. Active Instances (Core) - The Instances of the Launch Agent 4 Liquidity Layer with Active Status are stored herein. The RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage status defines whether the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model (see A.3.3 - Fully Implemented Risk Models ) or a pending risk model (see A.3.3 - Pending Risk Models ). If the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a fully implemented risk model the status is Covered . If the Instance Financial RRC is calculated based on a pending risk model the status is Pending . Ethereum Mainnet Instances (Core) - The Ethereum Mainnet Instances of the Launch Agent 4 Liquidity Layer with Active Status are stored herein and are organized by target protocol. Maple (Core) - The Ethereum Mainnet Instances of the Maple Protocol with Active Status are stored herein. Ethereum Mainnet - Maple USDC Instance Configuration Document (Core) - The documents herein contain the Instance Configuration Document for the Maple USDC Instance. RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage (Core) - Covered Parameters (Core) - The documents herein define the parameters of the Maple USDC Instance of the Allocation System Primitive. Instance Identifiers (Core) - The documents herein define the Instance identifiers. Network (Core) - Ethereum Mainnet Target Protocol (Core) - Maple Asset Supplied By Launch Agent 4 Liquidity Layer (Core) - USDC Token (Core) - syrupUSDC Contract Addresses (Core) - The documents herein define the Instance contract addresses. Token Address (Core) - 0x80ac24aA929eaF5013f6436cdA2a7ba190f5Cc0b Underlying Asset Address (Core) - 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48 RateLimitIDs (Core) - The specific RateLimitID (s) for this conduit’s inflow and outflow will be specified in a future iteration of the Launch Agent 4 Artifact. Inflow RateLimitID (Core) - The inflow RateLimitID is: 0x99a69e57b2f387f999d6adff6eb2e707b59fdb54f06ca6211b4f20956e9bfe10 Outflow RateLimitID (Core) - The outflow RateLimitID is: 0x64e6fd9d694640eebeeefc7b5abe32ef09bbabaa3d4e60221461d05a9577dc57 Rate Limits (Core) - The current maxAmount and slope for this conduit’s inflow/outflow are defined in the documents herein. Deposit Rate Limits (Core) - The deposit rate limits are: • maxAmount : 100,000,000 USDC per day • slope : 20,000,000 USDC per day Withdrawal Rate Limits (Core) - The withdrawal rate limits are: • maxAmount : Unlimited • slope : 0 Off-chain Operational Parameters (Core) - The documents herein contain specific off-chain parameters for this Instance. Instance-specific Operational Processes (Core) - The documents herein contain operational procedures or monitoring requirements unique to this Instance that deviate from or otherwise supplement the general Launch Agent 4 Liquidity Layer processes. Redeem Maple Shares (Core) - The documents herein define the steps for a relayer to redeem vault shares from Maple. Call RequestMapleRedemption Function (Core) - Only an operator with the relayer role can request the redemption of shares from Maple. To do so, they must call the requestMapleRedemption function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the Maple token address and the number of shares to request. All Maple redemption operations are performed on behalf of the ALM Proxy and the destination address is always set to the proxy by the contract. Calling this function will carry out the following actions: The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert. The contract will ensure the redemption amount is within the allowed rate limit for the specified vault and decrease the rate limit for the redemption amount. The contract will submit a redemption request to the vault. Assets will not be received immediately; they must be claimed in a separate step after the vault processes the redemption. The function call is as follows: function requestMapleRedemption(address mapleToken, uint256 shares) external Call CancelMapleRedemption Function (Core) - Only an operator with the relayer role can cancel a previously requested redemption of shares from Maple. To do so, they must call the cancelMapleRedemption function on the Controller contract on mainnet, providing the Maple token address and the number of shares to cancel. All Maple cancellations of redemption operations are performed on behalf of the ALM Proxy. Calling this function will carry out the following actions: The contract will confirm the relayer status of the operator. If the caller does not have the relayer role, the transaction will revert. The contract will check that a rate limit exists for the asset. If no rate limit exists the transaction will revert. The contract will submit a cancellation request to the vault, removing the specified number of shares from the pending redemption. The function call is as follows: function cancelMapleRedemption(address mapleToken, uint256 shares) external Completed Instances (Core) - The Instances of the Launch Agent 4 Liquidity Layer with Completed Status are stored herein. In Progress Invocations (Core) - The in progress Invocations of the Allocation System Primitive are contained herein. Once an Invocation is successfully completed, its subtree will be moved to Active Instances.

firstSeen.title: 2025-05-26 Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the following proposal to prepare for the launch of the SPK token. This proposal contains the following edits: Build Out Allocation System Primitive - Builds out the Allocation System Primitive, including the process for Star Agents to comply with the risk framework. Add Spark - Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Spark and Launch Agent 1. Add Sky - Spark / Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Sky, Spark, and Launch Agent 1. Add Logic Regarding Key Interest Rates - Adds logic regarding how the Base Rate is set and how it relates to the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Update Risk Framework - Updates the risk framework to include a new model for lending markets and models for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk. Rename First Loss Capital To Junior Risk Capital - Renames First Loss Capital to Junior Risk Capital to better align with other terminology in the Atlas. Update Logic Regarding Distribution Of Agent Tokens - Clarifies the distribution of Agent Tokens received by Sky under an Ecosystem Accord. Update Spark Liquidity Layer Documentation - Updates the documentation of the Spark Liquidity Layer to reflect that it is an implementation of the Allocation System Primitive. Update Spark Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates Spark Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Spark. Update Launch Agent 1 Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates the Launch Agent 1 Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Launch Agent 1. Given the size of the proposal, we are following the same approach that we used for the Agent Launch. First, we have published the proposal to a public Notion page: [Public] Atlas Edit Weekly Proposal For SPK Launch . Second, we have generated an HTML version of the Proposal; this allows us to guarantee that the Proposal submitted herein is immutable - it cannot be altered. We have attached the HTML file to the Notion page linked above. Simply click on the file, and your browser will download it. Please note: due to a Notion bug, internal references in the Proposal are not displayed correctly in the HTML file. To see the internal references and get the best experience, we would recommend that community members review the Notion page. Using the process below, community members can independently verify the contents of the Proposal submitted herein: Download the HTML file from the Notion page Open it in an editor such as VS Code Copy the contents into the hash generator at Keccak-256 - Online Tools Verify that the hash is equal to bedf45dceb0748041815e6a534eba006a83d00aded64c96b0d2ee7ac297f199d

This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas. Core GovOps validates the Star Agent’s reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Star Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of “eligible assets” for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See A.3.3 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC) . For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Star, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components. Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Star Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Star Agent’s TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Star Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations. Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Star Agent’s compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)). firstSeen.title: 2025-05-26 Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the following proposal to prepare for the launch of the SPK token. This proposal contains the following edits: Build Out Allocation System Primitive - Builds out the Allocation System Primitive, including the process for Star Agents to comply with the risk framework. Add Spark - Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Spark and Launch Agent 1. Add Sky - Spark / Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Sky, Spark, and Launch Agent 1. Add Logic Regarding Key Interest Rates - Adds logic regarding how the Base Rate is set and how it relates to the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Update Risk Framework - Updates the risk framework to include a new model for lending markets and models for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk. Rename First Loss Capital To Junior Risk Capital - Renames First Loss Capital to Junior Risk Capital to better align with other terminology in the Atlas. Update Logic Regarding Distribution Of Agent Tokens - Clarifies the distribution of Agent Tokens received by Sky under an Ecosystem Accord. Update Spark Liquidity Layer Documentation - Updates the documentation of the Spark Liquidity Layer to reflect that it is an implementation of the Allocation System Primitive. Update Spark Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates Spark Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Spark. Update Launch Agent 1 Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates the Launch Agent 1 Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Launch Agent 1. Given the size of the proposal, we are following the same approach that we used for the Agent Launch. First, we have published the proposal to a public Notion page: [Public] Atlas Edit Weekly Proposal For SPK Launch . Second, we have generated an HTML version of the Proposal; this allows us to guarantee that the Proposal submitted herein is immutable - it cannot be altered. We have attached the HTML file to the Notion page linked above. Simply click on the file, and your browser will download it. Please note: due to a Notion bug, internal references in the Proposal are not displayed correctly in the HTML file. To see the internal references and get the best experience, we would recommend that community members review the Notion page. Using the process below, community members can independently verify the contents of the Proposal submitted herein: Download the HTML file from the Notion page Open it in an editor such as VS Code Copy the contents into the hash generator at Keccak-256 - Online Tools Verify that the hash is equal to bedf45dceb0748041815e6a534eba006a83d00aded64c96b0d2ee7ac297f199d

lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Rename Star Agents To Prime Agents - Renames Star Agents to Prime Agents to prepare for the introduction of Halo Agents. Rename Prime Delegates To Ranked Delegates - Renames Prime Delegates to Ranked Delegates to avoid potential confusion given the introduction of Prime Agents. Update Ethena Risk Capital Requirements - Updates the near-term Required Risk Capital for Ethena exposures. Refine Risk Requirements For Real World Assets - Refines the Risk Framework requirements for investments in JTRSY and JAAA. Clarify Operator Of Spark Liquidity Layer - Clarifies that Spark has overall responsibility for the operation of the Spark Liquidity Layer. Remove Logic For DDM Vaults From Sky Core Atlas - Removes logic for the deprecated Morpho Dai DDM Vault from the Sky Core Atlas. Use Consistent Terminology For Administrative Risk - Updates references to “Admin Risk” to “Administrative Risk” for consistency. Make Follow Up Changes From August 4th Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal - Updates terminology used in the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation and clarifies the assets that qualify as Resting versus Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Rename Star Agents To Prime Agents Update the term Stars with Primes as specified in the linked Pull Request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/39 Rename Prime Delegates To Ranked Delegates Update the term Prime Delegates with Ranked Delegates as specified in the linked Pull Request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/40 Update Ethena Risk Capital Requirements Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.1.1.2 - Instance Total RRC (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Total RRC (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.1.1.2.1 - Application To Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Application To Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments and before A.3.3.1.1.2.2 - Incorporation Of Additional Types Of RRC (Portal) / A.3.3 - Incorporation Of Additional Types Of RRC (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Application To Ethena (Core) - In the short term, direct Ethena exposures automatically have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. In the long term, given the similarity of these assets to Real World Assets, adapted frameworks for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk for these exposures must be developed. See A.3.3 - Long Term Application To Real World Assets . Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.1.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for perpetual positions, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: Direct Ethena exposure - 2% Instance Financial RRC Ratio Indirect Ethena exposure through lending markets - 3% Instance Financial RRC Ratio For indirect Ethena exposure through lending markets, only the portion of the exposure to the lending market that is backed by Ethena-related assets (including PT-USDe, PT-sUSDe, and PT-eUSDe) is subject to the Instance Financial RRC Ratio specified above. The Instance Financial RRC Ratio for the remaining portion of the exposure is calculated based on the nature of the assets backing the exposure. Refine Risk Requirements For Real World Assets Replace A.3.3.1.1.2.1.1 - Short Term Application To Real World Asset (Portal) / A.3.3 - Short Term Application To Real World Assets (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Short Term Application To Real World Assets (Core) - In the short term, investments in the following Real World Assets automatically have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero: BUIDL JTRSY through Centrifuge v2 USTB JAAA through Centrifuge v2 JTRSY and JAAA through Centrifuge v3 once audits have been approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead All other investments in RWAs have Instance Total RRC of 100%. Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.4.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) and its subdocument to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for Real World Assets, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: BUIDL, JTRSY on Ethereum Mainnet, and USTB - 0% Instance Financial RRC Ratio JTRSY on Avalanche - 0.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio JAAA on Ethereum Mainnet - 1.6% Instance Financial RRC Ratio JAAA on Avalanche - 2.1% Instance Financial RRC Ratio In the near term, only the assets specified in A.3.3 - Short Term Application To Real World Assets will be eligible for investment under this provision. All other investments in Real World Assets have a 100% Instance Total RRC as specified in the document cited above. A.3.3 - Additional Restrictions On Investments In JTRSY And JAAA On Avalanche (Core) - Investments in JTRSY and JAAA on Avalanche are subject to the following additional restrictions: The initial deployment of capital into JTRSY and JAAA on Avalanche may not exceed 20 million USDS in total; Each additional deployment of capital into JTRSY or JAAA must be approved by the Stability Scope Advisors; Until audits of Centrifuge v3 are approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, the Prime must be below a 90% Risk Tolerance Ratio on a pro forma basis assuming that each additional deployment of capital into JTRSY and JAAA requires 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments in JTRSY and JAAA on Avalanche may not exceed 250 million USDS. Clarify Operator Of Spark Liquidity Layer Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.3 - Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management (Portal) / Spark - Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management (GitHub) to read as follows: Spark’s Operation Of Spark Liquidity Layer And Agreement Regarding Risk Tolerance Ratio - Spark will continue to operate the Spark Liquidity Layer and agrees to stay at or below a 90% Risk Tolerance Ratio. See A.3.3 - Risk Tolerance Ratio . Spark’s Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management Processes - As operators of the Spark Liquidity Layer, Spark automatically inherits, and is subject to, the base class of operational requirements related to Total Risk Capital management defined in A.2.4 - Primes’ Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management . Modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to the Spark Artifact. Remove Logic For DDM Vaults From Sky Core Atlas Delete A.3.5.5.3 - Morpho Vaults (Portal) / A.3.5 - Real World Assets - Perpetual Yield Strategies - Morpho Vaults (GitHub) and its subdocuments. Use Consistent Terminology For Administrative Risk Update the terms admin risk with administrative risk and admin rrc with administrative rrc as specified in the linked Pull Request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/41 Make Follow Up Changes From August 4th Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal Replace A.2.5.1.2.1.1.2.2.1.1 - Instance Expense (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives - Step 2: Calculate Total Allocation System Profit - Instance Profit - Instance Expense (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Instance Expense (Core) - Instance Expense for an Allocation System Instance for a month is the interest expense on the funds from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio invested in the Instance. It is calculated on a per block basis based on the amount invested from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio and the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Replace A.2.5.1.2.1.1.2.3.1 - Distortion Penalty (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives - Step 3: Calculate Adjusted Allocation System Profit - Distortion Penalty (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Distortion Penalty (Core) - The Distortion Penalty is a discretionary penalty designed to mitigate the potential misalignment caused by the asymmetric nature of the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation, where Primes earn profits on Allocation System Instances that earn more than the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate but do not suffer losses when Instances earn less than the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may assess a penalty of up to 100% of Total Allocation System Profit (see A.2.6 - Step 2: Calculate Total Allocation System Profit ) if it determines that a Prime’s decisions were distorted by this incentive structure. Replace A.2.5.1.2.1.1.2.3.2.1.1 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives - Step 3: Calculate Adjusted Allocation System Profit - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty - Excess Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Percentage - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral is Actively Stabilizing Collateral (see A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral ) that earns less than the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Replace A.3.4.2.2.1.1.1 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Portal) / A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC in the LitePSM; USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; USDT in USDT/USDS Curve pool; USDC in GUNI 0.01%; and USDC in GUNI 0.05%. Replace A.3.4.2.2.1.2.1 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Portal) / A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC and USDT in Curve (not paired with USDS); USDC and USDT in Uniswap; USDC and USDT in SparkLend; USDC and USDT in Aave; USDC and USDT in Morpho; and USDC USDT in a Prime ALM Proxy. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may impose limitations on the size of exposures to these protocols or to specific pools within these protocols that qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral in order to prevent excessive risk to Sky.

Rename Prime Delegates To Ranked Delegates - Renames Prime Delegates to Ranked Delegates to avoid potential confusion given the introduction of Prime Agents. Update Ethena Risk Capital Requirements - Updates the near-term Required Risk Capital for Ethena exposures. Refine Risk Requirements For Real World Assets - Refines the Risk Framework requirements for investments in JTRSY and JAAA. Clarify Operator Of Spark Liquidity Layer - Clarifies that Spark has overall responsibility for the operation of the Spark Liquidity Layer. Remove Logic For DDM Vaults From Sky Core Atlas - Removes logic for the deprecated Morpho Dai DDM Vault from the Sky Core Atlas. Use Consistent Terminology For Administrative Risk - Updates references to “Admin Risk” to “Administrative Risk” for consistency. Make Follow Up Changes From August 4th Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal - Updates terminology used in the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation and clarifies the assets that qualify as Resting versus Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Rename Star Agents To Prime Agents Update the term Stars with Primes as specified in the linked Pull Request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/39 Rename Prime Delegates To Ranked Delegates Update the term Prime Delegates with Ranked Delegates as specified in the linked Pull Request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/40 Update Ethena Risk Capital Requirements Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.1.1.2 - Instance Total RRC (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Total RRC (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.1.1.2.1 - Application To Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Application To Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments and before A.3.3.1.1.2.2 - Incorporation Of Additional Types Of RRC (Portal) / A.3.3 - Incorporation Of Additional Types Of RRC (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Application To Ethena (Core) - In the short term, direct Ethena exposures automatically have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. In the long term, given the similarity of these assets to Real World Assets, adapted frameworks for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk for these exposures must be developed. See A.3.3 - Long Term Application To Real World Assets . Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.1.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for perpetual positions, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: Direct Ethena exposure - 2% Instance Financial RRC Ratio Indirect Ethena exposure through lending markets - 3% Instance Financial RRC Ratio For indirect Ethena exposure through lending markets, only the portion of the exposure to the lending market that is backed by Ethena-related assets (including PT-USDe, PT-sUSDe, and PT-eUSDe) is subject to the Instance Financial RRC Ratio specified above. The Instance Financial RRC Ratio for the remaining portion of the exposure is calculated based on the nature of the assets backing the exposure. Refine Risk Requirements For Real World Assets Replace A.3.3.1.1.2.1.1 - Short Term Application To Real World Asset (Portal) / A.3.3 - Short Term Application To Real World Assets (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Short Term Application To Real World Assets (Core) - In the short term, investments in the following Real World Assets automatically have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero: BUIDL JTRSY through Centrifuge v2 USTB JAAA through Centrifuge v2 JTRSY and JAAA through Centrifuge v3 once audits have been approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead All other investments in RWAs have Instance Total RRC of 100%. Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.4.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) and its subdocument to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for Real World Assets, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: BUIDL, JTRSY on Ethereum Mainnet, and USTB - 0% Instance Financial RRC Ratio JTRSY on Avalanche - 0.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio JAAA on Ethereum Mainnet - 1.6% Instance Financial RRC Ratio JAAA on Avalanche - 2.1% Instance Financial RRC Ratio In the near term, only the assets specified in A.3.3 - Short Term Application To Real World Assets will be eligible for investment under this provision. All other investments in Real World Assets have a 100% Instance Total RRC as specified in the document cited above. A.3.3 - Additional Restrictions On Investments In JTRSY And JAAA On Avalanche (Core) - Investments in JTRSY and JAAA on Avalanche are subject to the following additional restrictions: The initial deployment of capital into JTRSY and JAAA on Avalanche may not exceed 20 million USDS in total; Each additional deployment of capital into JTRSY or JAAA must be approved by the Stability Scope Advisors; Until audits of Centrifuge v3 are approved by the Protocol Security Workstream Lead, the Prime must be below a 90% Risk Tolerance Ratio on a pro forma basis assuming that each additional deployment of capital into JTRSY and JAAA requires 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments in JTRSY and JAAA on Avalanche may not exceed 250 million USDS. Clarify Operator Of Spark Liquidity Layer Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.3 - Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management (Portal) / Spark - Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management (GitHub) to read as follows: Spark’s Operation Of Spark Liquidity Layer And Agreement Regarding Risk Tolerance Ratio - Spark will continue to operate the Spark Liquidity Layer and agrees to stay at or below a 90% Risk Tolerance Ratio. See A.3.3 - Risk Tolerance Ratio . Spark’s Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management Processes - As operators of the Spark Liquidity Layer, Spark automatically inherits, and is subject to, the base class of operational requirements related to Total Risk Capital management defined in A.2.4 - Primes’ Total Risk Capital (TRC) Management . Modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to the Spark Artifact. Remove Logic For DDM Vaults From Sky Core Atlas Delete A.3.5.5.3 - Morpho Vaults (Portal) / A.3.5 - Real World Assets - Perpetual Yield Strategies - Morpho Vaults (GitHub) and its subdocuments. Use Consistent Terminology For Administrative Risk Update the terms admin risk with administrative risk and admin rrc with administrative rrc as specified in the linked Pull Request: https://github.com/sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas/pull/41 Make Follow Up Changes From August 4th Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal Replace A.2.5.1.2.1.1.2.2.1.1 - Instance Expense (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives - Step 2: Calculate Total Allocation System Profit - Instance Profit - Instance Expense (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Instance Expense (Core) - Instance Expense for an Allocation System Instance for a month is the interest expense on the funds from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio invested in the Instance. It is calculated on a per block basis based on the amount invested from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio and the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Replace A.2.5.1.2.1.1.2.3.1 - Distortion Penalty (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives - Step 3: Calculate Adjusted Allocation System Profit - Distortion Penalty (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Distortion Penalty (Core) - The Distortion Penalty is a discretionary penalty designed to mitigate the potential misalignment caused by the asymmetric nature of the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation, where Primes earn profits on Allocation System Instances that earn more than the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate but do not suffer losses when Instances earn less than the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may assess a penalty of up to 100% of Total Allocation System Profit (see A.2.6 - Step 2: Calculate Total Allocation System Profit ) if it determines that a Prime’s decisions were distorted by this incentive structure. Replace A.2.5.1.2.1.1.2.3.2.1.1 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives - Step 3: Calculate Adjusted Allocation System Profit - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty - Excess Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Percentage - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral is Actively Stabilizing Collateral (see A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral ) that earns less than the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Replace A.3.4.2.2.1.1.1 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Portal) / A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC in the LitePSM; USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; USDT in USDT/USDS Curve pool; USDC in GUNI 0.01%; and USDC in GUNI 0.05%. Replace A.3.4.2.2.1.2.1 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Portal) / A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC and USDT in Curve (not paired with USDS); USDC and USDT in Uniswap; USDC and USDT in SparkLend; USDC and USDT in Aave; USDC and USDT in Morpho; and USDC USDT in a Prime ALM Proxy. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may impose limitations on the size of exposures to these protocols or to specific pools within these protocols that qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral in order to prevent excessive risk to Sky.

The wrapper enforces an upper limit on the price of SKY for the purposes of SKY-Backed Borrowing, which is set to be the minimum value of: The current price reported by PIP_SKY. These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3.1 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Restrictions On Investments On Plume (Core) - Investments on Plume are subject to the following restrictions: Assets other than RWAs on Plume or being bridged to Plume require 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments on Plume may not exceed 125 million USDS.

A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3.1 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Restrictions On Investments On Plume (Core) - Investments on Plume are subject to the following restrictions: Assets other than RWAs on Plume or being bridged to Plume require 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments on Plume may not exceed 125 million USDS.

firstSeen.title: 2025-05-26 Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the following proposal to prepare for the launch of the SPK token. This proposal contains the following edits: Build Out Allocation System Primitive - Builds out the Allocation System Primitive, including the process for Star Agents to comply with the risk framework. Add Spark - Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Spark and Launch Agent 1. Add Sky - Spark / Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Sky, Spark, and Launch Agent 1. Add Logic Regarding Key Interest Rates - Adds logic regarding how the Base Rate is set and how it relates to the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Update Risk Framework - Updates the risk framework to include a new model for lending markets and models for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk. Rename First Loss Capital To Junior Risk Capital - Renames First Loss Capital to Junior Risk Capital to better align with other terminology in the Atlas. Update Logic Regarding Distribution Of Agent Tokens - Clarifies the distribution of Agent Tokens received by Sky under an Ecosystem Accord. Update Spark Liquidity Layer Documentation - Updates the documentation of the Spark Liquidity Layer to reflect that it is an implementation of the Allocation System Primitive. Update Spark Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates Spark Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Spark. Update Launch Agent 1 Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates the Launch Agent 1 Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Launch Agent 1. Given the size of the proposal, we are following the same approach that we used for the Agent Launch. First, we have published the proposal to a public Notion page: [Public] Atlas Edit Weekly Proposal For SPK Launch . Second, we have generated an HTML version of the Proposal; this allows us to guarantee that the Proposal submitted herein is immutable - it cannot be altered. We have attached the HTML file to the Notion page linked above. Simply click on the file, and your browser will download it. Please note: due to a Notion bug, internal references in the Proposal are not displayed correctly in the HTML file. To see the internal references and get the best experience, we would recommend that community members review the Notion page. Using the process below, community members can independently verify the contents of the Proposal submitted herein: Download the HTML file from the Notion page Open it in an editor such as VS Code Copy the contents into the hash generator at Keccak-256 - Online Tools Verify that the hash is equal to bedf45dceb0748041815e6a534eba006a83d00aded64c96b0d2ee7ac297f199d

Update Risk Framework And Asset Liability Management Framework Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.1.1 - Near Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for perpetual positions, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: • Direct Ethena exposure - 3% Instance Financial RRC Ratio • Indirect Ethena exposure through lending markets - 4% Instance Financial RRC Ratio • All other protocols - 4% Instance Financial RRC Ratio For indirect Ethena exposure through lending markets, only the portion of the exposure to the lending market that is backed by Ethena-related assets (including PT-USDe, PT-sUSDe, and PT-eUSDe) is subject to the Instance Financial RRC Ratio specified above. The Instance Financial RRC Ratio for the remaining portion of the exposure is calculated based on the nature of the assets backing the exposure. Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.3.1 - Near Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for bond-like exposures, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: • PT-USDS - 0% Instance Financial RRC Ratio • All other bond-like exposures - 4% Instance Financial RRC Ratio In the near term, only Pendle PT tokens will be eligible for investment under this provision. These deployments will be subject to the approval of Operational GovOps. Correct Issues In The SPK Launch Proposal Replace A.2.3.9.1.1.2.2.1.3.2.1 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (Portal) / A.2.4 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (Core) -Core GovOps receives TRC Reports from Stars on a regular basis and must perform the following validation process. Core GovOps verifies against the Atlas any Ecosystem Accord referenced in the TRC Report for sourced Star-External Junior Risk Capital (SEJRC) or rented Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas. Core GovOps validates the Star Agent’s reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Star Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of “eligible assets” for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See A.3.3 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC) . For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Star, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components. Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Star Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Star Agent’s TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Star Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations. Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Star Agent’s compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)). lastEdit.title: 2025-05-26 Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal
lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the following proposal to prepare for the launch of the SPK token. This proposal contains the following edits: Build Out Allocation System Primitive - Builds out the Allocation System Primitive, including the process for Star Agents to comply with the risk framework. Add Spark - Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Spark and Launch Agent 1. Add Sky - Spark / Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Sky, Spark, and Launch Agent 1. Add Logic Regarding Key Interest Rates - Adds logic regarding how the Base Rate is set and how it relates to the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Update Risk Framework - Updates the risk framework to include a new model for lending markets and models for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk. Rename First Loss Capital To Junior Risk Capital - Renames First Loss Capital to Junior Risk Capital to better align with other terminology in the Atlas. Update Logic Regarding Distribution Of Agent Tokens - Clarifies the distribution of Agent Tokens received by Sky under an Ecosystem Accord. Update Spark Liquidity Layer Documentation - Updates the documentation of the Spark Liquidity Layer to reflect that it is an implementation of the Allocation System Primitive. Update Spark Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates Spark Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Spark. Update Launch Agent 1 Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates the Launch Agent 1 Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Launch Agent 1. Given the size of the proposal, we are following the same approach that we used for the Agent Launch. First, we have published the proposal to a public Notion page: [Public] Atlas Edit Weekly Proposal For SPK Launch . Second, we have generated an HTML version of the Proposal; this allows us to guarantee that the Proposal submitted herein is immutable - it cannot be altered. We have attached the HTML file to the Notion page linked above. Simply click on the file, and your browser will download it. Please note: due to a Notion bug, internal references in the Proposal are not displayed correctly in the HTML file. To see the internal references and get the best experience, we would recommend that community members review the Notion page. Using the process below, community members can independently verify the contents of the Proposal submitted herein: Download the HTML file from the Notion page Open it in an editor such as VS Code Copy the contents into the hash generator at Keccak-256 - Online Tools Verify that the hash is equal to bedf45dceb0748041815e6a534eba006a83d00aded64c96b0d2ee7ac297f199d

Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate - Increases the Required Risk Capital Percentage for USCC. Add Near Term Logic For Plume - Adds near term risk requirements for Plume to support Grove’s investment into ACRDX. The wrapper enforces an upper limit on the price of SKY for the purposes of SKY-Backed Borrowing, which is set to be the minimum value of: The current price reported by PIP_SKY. The cap that has been set on the OSM wrapper contract. A.4.4 - Cap Parameter (Core) - The subdocuments herein further describe the cap parameter and the process for its modification. The OSM wrapper uses the minimum value of the cap or the PIP_SKY oracle price to determine the price utilized for SKY-backed borrowing. Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3.1 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Restrictions On Investments On Plume (Core) - Investments on Plume are subject to the following restrictions: Assets other than RWAs on Plume or being bridged to Plume require 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments on Plume may not exceed 125 million USDS.
