The Instance Financial RRC for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3.1 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Restrictions On Investments On Plume (Core) - Investments on Plume are subject to the following restrictions: Assets other than RWAs on Plume or being bridged to Plume require 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments on Plume may not exceed 125 million USDS.

lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Change Funding Source For Accessibility Reward Wallet - Updates the Accessibility Reward wallet to be funded by Executive Votes rather than the Launch Project. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates - Allows Spark delegates to disclose conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation instead of publicly to avoid compromising anonymity. Add pyUSD To Risk Framework - Adds rules for RRC and ASC for investments in pyUSD to the Risk Framework. Clarify Approval Requirements For Agent Root Edits - Makes minor edits to clarify approval threshold for Agent Root Edits and handling of abstentions. Move Authority For Approving Additional Lending Markets To The Core Executor Agents - Moves the authority for approving additional lending markets to the Core Executor Agents. Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process - Updates the SparkLend multisig and clarifies the governance process for updates to multisig signers. Correct Responsible Party For Updating Active Data - Corrects the Responsible Party for updating some Active Data to be Operational GovOps rather than the Operational Facilitator. Complete Renaming Of “Star” To “Prime” - Replaces remaining references in the Atlas to “Star” with “Prime”. Change Funding Source For Accessibility Reward Wallet Replace A.2.3.8.1.2.1.4.3.1 - Near Term Process (Portal) / A.2.4 - Near Term Process (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Near-Term Process (Core) - In the near term, DAOcraft calculates the Accessibility Reward on behalf of the Support Facilitators. The Accessibility Facilitators then pay the Accessibility Reward from the Accessibility Reward Controller Wallet located on the Ethereum Mainnet at 0x05f471262d15eeca4059dade070e5bed509a4e73 within seven (7) days of the end of every month. The balance of this wallet may be topped up to 3 million USDS. This funding is subject to an Executive Vote. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.3.1.3.3.4 - Abstain Only for Disclosed Conflicts (Portal) / Spark - Abstain Only for Disclosed Conflicts (GitHub) to read as follows: Disclosure Of Conflicts (Core) - Conflicts must be disclosed to the Spark Foundation before the voting window (see Root Edit Token Holder Vote ) for the proposal begins. Abstaining For Non-Disclosed Conflicts (Core) - Abstaining for any reason other than a disclosed conflict is treated as non-performance under Delegate Offboarding . Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.4.2.2 - Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (Portal) / Spark - Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (GitHub) to read as follows: Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (Core) - At onboarding, prospective Delegates must provide any known conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation. Disclosures must be updated as new conflicts arise. Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.8 - Registry of Delegates (Portal) / Spark - Registry of Delegates (GitHub) to read as follows: Registry of Delegates (Core) - The subdocuments herein list each active Delegate’s name, wallet address, effective date, and status. Entries are maintained via an Active Data document updated by the Operational Facilitator. Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.8.1 - Template Information For Each Delegate (Portal) / Spark - Template Information For Each Delegate (GitHub) to read as follows: Template Information For Each Delegate (Core) - The list of Delegates must follow this template for each recorded Delegate: [Insert Delegate Handle] Delegate Name: [Insert Handle] Delegate Wallet Address: Effective Date: Status: Active/Inactive/Suspended Add pyUSD To Risk Framework Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.6.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for Cash Stablecoins, a 0% Instance Financial RRC will be applied to Cash Stablecoins. In the near term, only USDS, sUSDS, Dai, sDai, USDC, USDT, and pyUSD (either held directly or through decentralized exchanges such as Curve) will be eligible for investment under this provision. Add a new subdocument of A.3.4.2.1 - Definitions (Portal) / A.3.4 - Definitions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.4.2.1.2 - Low Risk Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.4 - Low Risk Real World Assets (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Cash Stablecoins (Core) - Cash Stablecoins are defined as USDC, USDT, and pyUSD. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.4.2.2.1 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements. A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC in the LitePSM; USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; Cash Stablecoins in Curve (paired with USDS); USDC in GUNI 0.01%; and USDC in GUNI 0.05%. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral consists of Cash Stablecoins that do not qualify as Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral but can be converted to Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may include Cash Stablecoins deposited into lending protocols, Cash Stablecoins used to provide liquidity to decentralized exchanges, or liquid staking derivatives of cash stablecoins. Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral: The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles; The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: Cash Stablecoins in Curve (not paired with USDS); Cash Stablecoins in Uniswap; Cash Stablecoins in SparkLend; Cash Stablecoins in Aave; Cash Stablecoins in Morpho; and Cash Stablecoins in a Prime ALM Proxy. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may impose limitations on the size of exposures to these protocols or to specific pools within these protocols that qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral in order to prevent excessive risk to Sky. A.3.4 - Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Clarify Approval Requirements For Agent Root Edits Replace A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Spark - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Spark Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. Token holders may vote directly or through Delegates. See Delegation Framework . The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. Delete A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.2.1 - Circulating Supply Definition (Portal) / Spark - Circulating Supply Definition (GitHub) . Replace A.AG2.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Grove - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Grove Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. Replace A.AG3.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Launch Agent 2 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Launch Agent 2 Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. Replace A.AG4.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Launch Agent 3 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Launch Agent 3 Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. Move Authority For Approving Additional Lending Markets To The Core Executor Agents Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.1.2 - Covered Protocols (Portal) / A.3.3 - Covered Protocols (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Covered Protocols (Core) - The calculation of Instance Financial RRC for lending markets is applicable to the following protocols: Aave v2 Aave v3 SparkLend Morpho Maple The application by a Prime Agent of the Risk Framework for lending markets to any protocols not listed above must be approved by the Core Executor Agents. The Core Executor Agents shall consult with the Stability Scope Advisors and the Stability Facilitators in making this determination. Any such approval must be posted to the Sky Forum under the category for the Prime Agent. Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process Replace A.1.9.3.1.1.2 - SparkLend Multisig Number Of Signers (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Number Of Signers (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Number Of Signers (Core) - The SparkLend Security Access Multisig currently has a 3/5 signing requirement. Replace A.1.9.3.1.1.3 - SparkLend Multisig Current Signers (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Current Signers (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Current Signers (Core) - The SparkLend Security Access Multisig currently has the following signers: VoteWizard LDR Hexonaut MonetSupply LucasManuel Replace A.1.9.3.1.1.4 - SparkLend Multisig Signer Modifications (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Signer Modifications (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Signer Modifications (Core) - Modification of the signers of the SparkLend Security Access Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required. The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll. Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. The Governance Facilitators should consider preparing an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig. Replace A.AG1.2.6.P15.2.1.2.2.3.5 - Modification (Portal) / Spark - Modification (GitHub) to read as follows: Modification - Modification of the signers of the Freezer Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required. The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. In both cases, the signer is required to communicate the loss of access to their private key, or the wish to be removed as a signer, in the form of a public Sky Forum post. The specific signer should be replaced as soon as possible, which does not require a Governance Poll. Any changes to the multisig signers that do not fall within the two exceptions listed above, or that have not been ratified by Sky Governance, should be questioned immediately and treated as malicious. Where malicious activity is suspected, the Governance Facilitators must prepare an expedited Executive Vote so that Sky Governance can vote on removing external security access from the multisig. Correct Responsible Party For Updating Active Data Replace A.2.3.8.1.2.3.6.4.1.1 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (Portal) / A.2.4 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (Core) - A.2.4 - List Of Onboarding Integrators is updated as follows: Updated fields Onboarding Integrators New value: Delete the Integrator. Responsible Party: Operational GovOps Triggers: None Replace A.2.3.8.1.2.3.6.4.1.2 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (Portal) / A.2.4 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (Core) - A.2.4 - List Of Current Integrators is updated as follows: Updated fields Current Integrators New value: set to the name of the Integrator from the approved Proposal Reward Code New value: set to the Reward Code from the approved Proposal Tracking Methodology New value: set to the tracking methodology from the approved Proposal Responsible Party: Operational GovOps Triggers: None Replace A.2.3.8.2.2.3.6.4.1.1 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (Portal) / A.2.4 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (Core) - A.2.4 - List Of Onboarding Integrators is updated as follows: Updated fields Onboarding Integrators New value: Delete the Integrator. Responsible Party: Operational GovOps Triggers: None Replace A.2.3.8.2.2.3.6.4.1.2 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (Portal) / A.2.4 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (Core) - A.2.4 - List Of Current Integrators is updated as follows: Updated fields Current Integrators New value: set to the name of the Integrator from the approved Proposal Reward Code New value: set to the Reward Code from the approved Proposal Tracking Methodology New value: set to the tracking methodology from the approved Proposal Responsible Party: Operational GovOps Triggers: None Complete Renaming Of “Star” To “Prime” Update the term Stars with Primes as specified in the linked Pull Request: Forthcoming Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal by aa-lex · Pull Request #50 · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub

firstSeen.title: 2025-10-06 Weekly Edit Proposal
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. Note that due to the size of the proposal it will be split into multiple posts. This proposal includes the following edits: Introduce Keel - Updates references from Launch Agent 2 to Keel now that Keel has publicly launched. Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle - Specifies that Amatsu will only prepare the Initial Calculation with respect to Spark for the October Monthly Settlement Cycle. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation - Adds an expected timeline of January 1, 2026 for Stage 2 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital - Clarifies the definition of Genesis Capital for the Genesis Capital Backstop. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper - Defines the Capped SKY Oracle wrapper to prepare for the launch of stUSDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs - Allows Prime Agents to invest directly in Pendle PTs backed by Ethena Exposures and defines the Required Risk Capital for doing so. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets - Implements an Equivalent Loss framework for Real World Assets to reflect the lower risk of these assets due to the possibility of recovery through legal recourse. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate - Increases the Required Risk Capital Percentage for USCC. Add Near Term Logic For Plume - Adds near term risk requirements for Plume to support Grove’s investment into ACRDX. Define The Executive Process - Adds an initial end-to-end process definition for the Sky Executive Process. Introduce Keel Update references to Launch Agent 2 and minor related edits as specified in the linked Pull Request: Forthcoming Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal by aa-lex · Pull Request #65 · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle Add a new subdocument of A.2.5.1.2.1.6 - Interim Measures (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Process Definition - Interim Measures (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.2.5.1.2.1.6.2 - Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Process Definition - Interim Measures - Process For September 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.6 - Process For October 2025 Monthly Settlement Cycle (Core) - For the Monthly Settlement Cycle conducted in October 2025, the Initial Calculation prepared by Operational Executor Agent Amatsu will only include calculations related to Spark. The Independent Calculation prepared by BA Labs on behalf of the Core Council will be prepared normally. The calculations related to Spark will be subject to the normal resolution process defined in A.2.6 - Resolution Of Differences By Core GovOps Atlas Axis . For all other calculations, the amounts in the Independent Calculation will be treated as Agreed Amounts. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation Replace A.2.5.1.2.2.2.2 - Stage 2 Timing (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Implementation Stages - Stage 2 - Stage 2 Timing (GitHub) to read as follows: Stage 2 Timing (Core) - Stage 2 is currently expected to be implemented in the February 2026 Monthly Settlement Cycle for the period from January 1, 2026 to January 31, 2026. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital Replace A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Core) - If a “SKY Backstop Event” is in progress and the SKY price equals zero, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized exactly to restore the Surplus Buffer to zero. Add a new subdocument of A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.8.1.5.5 - Genesis Agents (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Agents to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital (Core) - The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper Add new subdocuments of A.4.4.1.2 - SKY-Backed Borrowing (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.4.4.1.2.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper (Core) - In order to prevent excessive price spikes if there is high demand for leverage against SKY tokens, which could potentially lead to excessive USDS borrowing against SKY, a wrapper for the SKY OSM contract has been developed. The wrapper enforces an upper limit on the price of SKY for the purposes of SKY-Backed Borrowing, which is set to be the minimum value of: The current price reported by PIP_SKY. The cap that has been set on the OSM wrapper contract. A.4.4 - Cap Parameter (Core) - The subdocuments herein further describe the cap parameter and the process for its modification. A.4.4 - Definition (Core) - The cap parameter represents one of the potential inputs for the SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper. The OSM wrapper uses the minimum value of the cap or the PIP_SKY oracle price to determine the price utilized for SKY-backed borrowing. A.4.4 - Modification (Core) - The Core Facilitator, in consultation with BA Labs, has the ability to modify the cap parameter. The modification of said parameter is pursuant to the Operational Weekly Cycle and can be effected directly via an Executive Vote, without requiring a prior Governance Poll. A.4.4 - Current Value (Core) - The current value of the cap parameter is: 0.04 USDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Core) - Ethena Exposures consist of Direct Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures ), Indirect Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures ), and Pendle Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures). The Instance Financial RRC for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3.1 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Restrictions On Investments On Plume (Core) - Investments on Plume are subject to the following restrictions: Assets other than RWAs on Plume or being bridged to Plume require 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments on Plume may not exceed 125 million USDS.

Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital Replace A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Core) - If a “SKY Backstop Event” is in progress and the SKY price equals zero, the Sky Protocol must apply a pro‑rata haircut across each Genesis Agent’s Genesis Capital, implemented as a transfer of eligible assets from each Agent to the Sky Surplus Buffer. The haircut must be sized exactly to restore the Surplus Buffer to zero. Add a new subdocument of A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.8.1.5.5 - Genesis Agents (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Agents to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital (Core) - The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper Add new subdocuments of A.4.4.1.2 - SKY-Backed Borrowing (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.4.4.1.2.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper (Core) - In order to prevent excessive price spikes if there is high demand for leverage against SKY tokens, which could potentially lead to excessive USDS borrowing against SKY, a wrapper for the SKY OSM contract has been developed. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Core) - Ethena Exposures consist of Direct Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures ), Indirect Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures ), and Pendle Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures). Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.3.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.3.3.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - The Administrative RRC for BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.2.1 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 4.5% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. Add Near Term Logic For Plume Add a new subdocument of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.5.3.1 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Financial RRC Ratios For Specific Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Restrictions On Investments On Plume (Core) - Investments on Plume are subject to the following restrictions: Assets other than RWAs on Plume or being bridged to Plume require 100% Instance Total RRC; and Total investments on Plume may not exceed 125 million USDS.

lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Add Timeline For Transition Of Spark Governance Processes - Adds timeline for transferring control of Spark infrastructure from Sky Governance to Spark. Update Risk Framework And Asset Liability Management Framework - Updates risk framework and asset liability management framework for latest improvements recommended by BA Labs. Add Specifications For Spark Genesis Capital Allocation - Adds specifications for Spark Genesis Capital Allocation. Limit Accessibility Reward Bonus To End User Balances - Limits Spark and Launch Agent 1 from receiving Accessibility Reward bonus on USDS and sUSDS balances they hold. Authorize Launch Agent 2 Deployment Of Idle Cash - Authorizes Launch Agent 2 to deploy idle cash into lending markets on Solana subject to approval of its Operational Executor Agent. Correct Issues In The SPK Launch Proposal - Makes minor corrections to the Atlas following up on the SPK Launch. Update Spark Liquidity Layer - Adds Aave USDC on Base as an active Instance and corrects references and parameters. At such time, which is currently estimated for September 17, 2025, control will transition to Spark Governance. This transitionary measure ensures better decentralization of the SPK token before Spark Governance takes full control of the named parameters under the Root Edit Primitive. Update Risk Framework And Asset Liability Management Framework Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.1.1 - Near Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for perpetual positions, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: • Direct Ethena exposure - 3% Instance Financial RRC Ratio • Indirect Ethena exposure through lending markets - 4% Instance Financial RRC Ratio • All other protocols - 4% Instance Financial RRC Ratio For indirect Ethena exposure through lending markets, only the portion of the exposure to the lending market that is backed by Ethena-related assets (including PT-USDe, PT-sUSDe, and PT-eUSDe) is subject to the Instance Financial RRC Ratio specified above. The Instance Financial RRC Ratio for the remaining portion of the exposure is calculated based on the nature of the assets backing the exposure. Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.3.1 - Near Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for bond-like exposures, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: • PT-USDS - 0% Instance Financial RRC Ratio • All other bond-like exposures - 4% Instance Financial RRC Ratio In the near term, only Pendle PT tokens will be eligible for investment under this provision. These deployments will be subject to the approval of Operational GovOps. Correct Issues In The SPK Launch Proposal Replace A.2.3.9.1.1.2.2.1.3.2.1 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (Portal) / A.2.4 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (Core) -Core GovOps receives TRC Reports from Stars on a regular basis and must perform the following validation process. Core GovOps verifies against the Atlas any Ecosystem Accord referenced in the TRC Report for sourced Star-External Junior Risk Capital (SEJRC) or rented Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas. Core GovOps validates the Star Agent’s reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Star Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of “eligible assets” for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See A.3.3 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC) . For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Star, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components. Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Star Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Star Agent’s TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Star Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations. Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Star Agent’s compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)). lastEdit.title: 2025-05-26 Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal
lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the following proposal to prepare for the launch of the SPK token. This proposal contains the following edits: Build Out Allocation System Primitive - Builds out the Allocation System Primitive, including the process for Star Agents to comply with the risk framework. Add Spark - Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Spark and Launch Agent 1. Add Sky - Spark / Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Sky, Spark, and Launch Agent 1. Add Logic Regarding Key Interest Rates - Adds logic regarding how the Base Rate is set and how it relates to the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Update Risk Framework - Updates the risk framework to include a new model for lending markets and models for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk. Rename First Loss Capital To Junior Risk Capital - Renames First Loss Capital to Junior Risk Capital to better align with other terminology in the Atlas. Update Logic Regarding Distribution Of Agent Tokens - Clarifies the distribution of Agent Tokens received by Sky under an Ecosystem Accord. Update Spark Liquidity Layer Documentation - Updates the documentation of the Spark Liquidity Layer to reflect that it is an implementation of the Allocation System Primitive. Update Spark Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates Spark Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Spark. Update Launch Agent 1 Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates the Launch Agent 1 Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Launch Agent 1. Given the size of the proposal, we are following the same approach that we used for the Agent Launch. First, we have published the proposal to a public Notion page: [Public] Atlas Edit Weekly Proposal For SPK Launch . Second, we have generated an HTML version of the Proposal; this allows us to guarantee that the Proposal submitted herein is immutable - it cannot be altered. We have attached the HTML file to the Notion page linked above. Simply click on the file, and your browser will download it. Please note: due to a Notion bug, internal references in the Proposal are not displayed correctly in the HTML file. To see the internal references and get the best experience, we would recommend that community members review the Notion page. Using the process below, community members can independently verify the contents of the Proposal submitted herein: Download the HTML file from the Notion page Open it in an editor such as VS Code Copy the contents into the hash generator at Keccak-256 - Online Tools Verify that the hash is equal to bedf45dceb0748041815e6a534eba006a83d00aded64c96b0d2ee7ac297f199d

firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. Note that due to the size of the proposal it will be split into multiple posts. This proposal includes the following edits: Introduce Keel - Updates references from Launch Agent 2 to Keel now that Keel has publicly launched. Specify Near Term Logic For October Monthly Settlement Cycle - Specifies that Amatsu will only prepare the Initial Calculation with respect to Spark for the October Monthly Settlement Cycle. Specify Expected Timing For Stage 2 Of Monthly Settlement Cycle Implementation - Adds an expected timeline of January 1, 2026 for Stage 2 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Clarify Definition Of Genesis Capital - Clarifies the definition of Genesis Capital for the Genesis Capital Backstop. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper - Defines the Capped SKY Oracle wrapper to prepare for the launch of stUSDS. Allow Direct Investment In Pendle PTs - Allows Prime Agents to invest directly in Pendle PTs backed by Ethena Exposures and defines the Required Risk Capital for doing so. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets - Implements an Equivalent Loss framework for Real World Assets to reflect the lower risk of these assets due to the possibility of recovery through legal recourse. Increase Required Risk Capital For Superstate - Increases the Required Risk Capital Percentage for USCC. Add Near Term Logic For Plume - Adds near term risk requirements for Plume to support Grove’s investment into ACRDX. Define The Executive Process - Adds an initial end-to-end process definition for the Sky Executive Process. The haircut must be sized exactly to restore the Surplus Buffer to zero. Add a new subdocument of A.3.8.1.5 - Genesis Capital Backstop (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Capital Backstop (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.8.1.5.5 - Genesis Agents (Portal) / A.3.9 - Genesis Agents to read as follows: A.3.9 - Genesis Capital (Core) - The Genesis Capital of an Agent is the lesser of (1) the amount of capital contributed by Sky to the Agent and (2) the total capital of the Agent. Define Capped SKY Oracle Wrapper Add new subdocuments of A.4.4.1.2 - SKY-Backed Borrowing (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.4.4.1.2.8 - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (Portal) / A.4.4 - SKY Staking Mechanism - SKY Staking - SKY-Backed Borrowing - stUSDS Bounded External Access Module (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.4.4 - SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper (Core) - In order to prevent excessive price spikes if there is high demand for leverage against SKY tokens, which could potentially lead to excessive USDS borrowing against SKY, a wrapper for the SKY OSM contract has been developed. The wrapper enforces an upper limit on the price of SKY for the purposes of SKY-Backed Borrowing, which is set to be the minimum value of: The current price reported by PIP_SKY. The cap that has been set on the OSM wrapper contract. A.4.4 - Cap Parameter (Core) - The subdocuments herein further describe the cap parameter and the process for its modification. A.4.4 - Definition (Core) - The cap parameter represents one of the potential inputs for the SKY-Backed Borrowing Capped OSM Wrapper. The OSM wrapper uses the minimum value of the cap or the PIP_SKY oracle price to determine the price utilized for SKY-backed borrowing. A.4.4 - Modification (Core) - The Core Facilitator, in consultation with BA Labs, has the ability to modify the cap parameter. The Instance Financial RRC for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.1.2 - Indirect Ethena Exposures(Portal) / A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.3 - Pendle Ethena Exposures (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe. The Instance Financial RRC for Pendle Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Maturity Greater Than Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with more than six (6) months to maturity require 100% Instance Total RRC. A.3.3 - Maturity Less Than Or Equal To Six Months (Core) - Pendle Ethena Exposures with less than or equal to six (6) months to maturity have Instance Financial RRC calculated as follows: Instance Financial RRC = initialValue - ((currentTime - startTime) * decayRatePerSecond) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Initial Value (Core) - The Initial Value initialValue is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT has exactly six (6) months to maturity. The initialValue is 15%. A.3.3 - Current Time (Core) - The Current Time currentTime is the timestamp of the current Ethereum block. A.3.3 - Start Time (Core) - The Start Time startTime is the timestamp of the block exactly six (6) months before the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Decay Rate Per Second (Core) - The Decay Rate Per Second decayRatePerSecond is calculated as follows: decayRatePerSecond = totalDecay / totalDuration The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Total Decay (Core) - The Total Decay totalDecay is equal to the Initial Value minus the Final Value. A.3.3 - Final Value (Core) - The Final Value is the Instance Financial RRC when the PT is at maturity. Since the PT is convertible into the underlying asset at this point it is equal to the Instance Financial RRC for Direct Ethena Exposures specified in A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures . A.3.3 - Total Duration (Core) - The Total Duration totalDuration is equal to the Expiration Time minus the Start Time. A.3.3 - Expiration Time (Core) - The Expiration Time is the expiration timestamp of the PT. A.3.3 - Concentration Limit (Core) - Any investments made by Prime Agents in Pendle Ethena Exposures in excess of 20% of their total Allocation System Investments require 100% Instance Total RRC. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1.1.2 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital ) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,300,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Ethena Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Exposure Limit for each Agent is: Spark - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Grove - One half of the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit All other Prime Agents - Zero A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause its Ethena Exposures to exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If a Prime Agent’s Ethena Exposures exceed its Ethena Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct the Agent to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce its Ethena Exposures below its Ethena Exposure Limit. Implement Equivalent Loss Framework For Real World Assets Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.3 - Real World Assets (GitHub) and its subdocuments Add new subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.2.4 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.3.3 - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.3.3.2.1.2.4.2 - Ethena (Portal) / A.3.3 - Ethena (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, And JAAA (Core) - In the short term, investments in BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Administrative RRC of zero. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. It is calculated according to the following formula: Equivalent Loss = Raw Exposure * Expected Frozen Duration * Litigation Financing Costs The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - Raw Exposure is specified in A.3.3 - Raw Exposure. A.3.3 - Expected Frozen Duration (Core) - Expected Frozen Duration is the estimated time, in years or fractions thereof, that the Legal Recourse Asset would remain frozen after a hack or technical exploit before the holder would be able to recover the underlying assets through legal recourse. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. A.3.3 - Raw Exposure (Core) - The Raw Exposure is the total exposure to the particular Allocation System opportunity. A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Legal Recourse Assets. firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Add Timeline For Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract - Specifies when the Legacy Conversion Contract will be disabled. Refine SKY Rewards Rate Normalization Process - Provides the Governance Facilitators with greater flexibility in normalizing the effective yield for SKY Token Rewards. Update Spark Artifact And Ecosystem Accord To Prepare For SPK Launch - Updates Spark’s Agent Artifact and one of its Ecosystem Accords to prepare for the SPK launch. Add Timeline For Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract Replace A.4.1.2.2.4.2 - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Portal) / A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Github) to read as follows: A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Core) - The legacy MKR to SKY conversion contract (Legacy Conversion Contract) burns MKR and mints new SKY. The new MKR to SKY conversion contract (New Conversion Contract) instead burns MKR and issues SKY from the existing supply of preminted SKY. The Legacy Conversion Contract will be disabled as specified in 4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract. To offset SKY minted by the Legacy Conversion Contract after the deployment of the New Conversion Contract, an equivalent amount of preminted SKY will be burned. This action will ensure the total SKY token supply remains as if these specific emissions from the Legacy Conversion Contract had not occurred. A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract (Core) - The disabling of the Legacy Conversion Contract will be executed in the June 26, 2025 Executive Vote. This action is authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without a prior Governance Poll. Refine SKY Rewards Rate Normalization Process Replace A.4.3.2.1 - SKY Token Rewards (Portal) / A.4.3 - Savings Rate And Token Reward Mechanism - Token Reward Mechanism - SKY Token Rewards (Github) to read as follows: A.4.3 - Savings Rate And Token Reward Mechanism - Token Reward Mechanism - SKY Token Rewards (Core) - With each Executive Vote, the distribution of SKY token rewards to USDS holders is normalized to ensure the effective yield provided by these rewards equals the Sky Savings Rate (SSR) for the upcoming period. The effective yield is defined as: (Total Market Value of Distributed SKY Tokens / Total Eligible USDS Balance). To achieve this normalization, the quantity of SKY token rewards to be distributed is determined through the following calculation, performed for each normalization period: Determine Target Reward Value: Calculate the total US dollar value required to meet the SSR for the period: (Total Eligible USDS Balance * SSR). Determine SKY Token Quantity: Divide the Target Reward Value (from step 1) by the Current Market Price of SKY (determined at the time of the Executive Vote). The Governance Facilitators, on the recommendation of the Stability Scope Advisors, may maintain the quantity of SKY token rewards to be distributed for a normalization period at its current level if they conclude that: the difference between the effective yield provided by SKY Tokens Rewards and the SSR is not material; the difference between the effective yield provided by SKY Token Rewards and the SSR is unlikely to persist due to other factors; or adjusting the quantity of SKY Token Rewards is otherwise inadvisable. The recommendation of the Stability Scope Advisors must be posted to the Sky Forum and approved by the Stability Facilitators. Add new subdocuments of A.AG1.2.1.P4.2.1.1.7 - Custom Instance Parameters (Portal) / Spark - Custom Instance Parameters (Github) to read as follows: Staking (Core) - SPK token holders can stake their tokens. The rewards for staking will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.2.1.P4.2.1.2 - Operational Process Definition (Portal) / Spark - Operational Process Definition (Github) to read as follows: Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd (Core) - The Genesis Supply was minted to an account owned by SPK Company Ltd. The address of the account on the Ethereum Mainnet is 0x6FE588FDCC6A34207485cc6e47673F59cCEDF92B . Transfer Of Tokens To Sky (Core) - SPK Company Ltd transferred 6.5 billion SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Sky Pause Proxy. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. Transfer Of Tokens To Spark SubProxy Account (Core) - SPK Company Ltd transferred 918,760,451 SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Spark SubProxy Account. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. The Spark SubProxy Account is specified in SubProxy Account . Transfer Of Tokens To Spark Foundation (Core) - SPK Company Ltd will transfer 1 billion SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Spark Foundation. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. The address of the Spark Foundation on the Ethereum Mainnet will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Tokens Retained By SPK Company Ltd ( Core) - 1,581,239,549 SPK tokens will be retained by SPK Company Ltd. The use of these tokens will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1 - Routine Protocol (Portal) / Spark - Routine Protocol (Github) to read as follows: Root Edit Proposal Submission (Core) - The Root Edit process begins with a SPK token holder submitting a proposal through the Powerhouse system containing a draft Artifact Edit Proposal. A SPK token holder must hold at least 1% of the total token supply to submit a proposal. The proposal must also be posted on the Sky Forum under the “Spark” tag. Root Edit Proposal Submission Requirements Exception For Nested Contributors (Core) - Nested Contributors are always authorized to submit Artifact Edit Proposals and do not have to fulfill the token-holding requirements defined in Root Edit Proposal Submission. However, all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply. To see the Agent’s Nested Contributors, see Phoenix Labs. Root Edit Proposal Submission Requirements Exception For Spark Foundation (Core) - While it is a core service provider to Spark, the Spark Foundation is authorized to submit Artifact Edit Proposals and does not have to fulfill the token-holding requirements defined in Root Edit Proposal Submission. However, all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply. Short-Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - Until the Powerhouse system supports submitting Artifact Edit Proposals, SPK token holders may submit Artifact Edit Proposals by posting them to the Sky Forum under the “Spark” category. The title of the post must include the text “Spark Artifact Edit Proposal”. The post must include cryptographic proof that the author controls an account holding the required percentage of the total SPK token supply specified in Root Edit Proposal Submission. Root Edit Expert Advisor Review (Core) - A future iteration of the Spark Artifact will specify guidelines for obtaining specialized review of proposals requiring advanced technical or financial analysis. Root Edit Proposal Review By Operational Facilitator (Core) - Within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment. If the proposal is aligned, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding. In this Forum post, the Operational Facilitator must also confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize. If the proposal is misaligned, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding and provide the reasoning for it. Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Spark Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have 50% of votes in favor to be approved. Circulating Supply Definition (Core) - For purposes of Root Edit Token Holder Vote, the circulating supply of SPK tokens is equal to the total supply of SPK tokens minus the sum of: Tokens retained by SKY and not yet distributed as token rewards (see A.2.10 - Sky Retained Tokens And Reward Pools ); and Tokens retained in vesting agreements for Spark contributors and not yet distributed; and Tokens in the Spark SubProxy Account (see SubProxy Account ). Root Edit Artifact Update (Core) - At the conclusion of the poll, if the proposal is approved, the Operational Facilitator submits the edit to Powerhouse to formally update the Agent Artifact. Regardless of the outcome, the Operational Facilitator updates the Powerhouse System to include the result of the vote, including any pertinent documents. Short Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - Until the Powerhouse system supports updating Agent Artifacts, the Operational Facilitator works with the Governance Facilitators to update the Atlas GitHub repository located at Pull requests · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub to reflect proposals approved by Star Governance. Artifact Edit Restrictions (Core) - The Spark Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals. Time-Limited Root Edit Restrictions On Removal Of Nested Contributors (Core) - For a period of three years after June 4, 2025, any Artifact Edit that would have the effect of removing a Nested Contributor must be approved by a vote of SKY holders in addition to a vote of SPK holders to be effective. Add a new subdocument of A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2 - Operational Process Definition (Portal) / Spark - Operational Process Definition (Github) This document should be located directly after A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.3 - Emergency Protocol (Portal) / Spark - Emergency Protocol (Github) to read as follows: Short Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - In the short term, the parameters of the Spark Liquidity Layer, SparkLend, and Spark Savings are controlled by Sky Core, but will be transitioned to Spark in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. See SparkLend Risk Parameters Modification .
