lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Change Funding Source For Accessibility Reward Wallet - Updates the Accessibility Reward wallet to be funded by Executive Votes rather than the Launch Project. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates - Allows Spark delegates to disclose conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation instead of publicly to avoid compromising anonymity. Add pyUSD To Risk Framework - Adds rules for RRC and ASC for investments in pyUSD to the Risk Framework. Clarify Approval Requirements For Agent Root Edits - Makes minor edits to clarify approval threshold for Agent Root Edits and handling of abstentions. Move Authority For Approving Additional Lending Markets To The Core Executor Agents - Moves the authority for approving additional lending markets to the Core Executor Agents. Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process - Updates the SparkLend multisig and clarifies the governance process for updates to multisig signers. Correct Responsible Party For Updating Active Data - Corrects the Responsible Party for updating some Active Data to be Operational GovOps rather than the Operational Facilitator. Complete Renaming Of “Star” To “Prime” - Replaces remaining references in the Atlas to “Star” with “Prime”. Change Funding Source For Accessibility Reward Wallet Replace A.2.3.8.1.2.1.4.3.1 - Near Term Process (Portal) / A.2.4 - Near Term Process (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Near-Term Process (Core) - In the near term, DAOcraft calculates the Accessibility Reward on behalf of the Support Facilitators. The Accessibility Facilitators then pay the Accessibility Reward from the Accessibility Reward Controller Wallet located on the Ethereum Mainnet at 0x05f471262d15eeca4059dade070e5bed509a4e73 within seven (7) days of the end of every month. The balance of this wallet may be topped up to 3 million USDS. This funding is subject to an Executive Vote. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.3.1.3.3.4 - Abstain Only for Disclosed Conflicts (Portal) / Spark - Abstain Only for Disclosed Conflicts (GitHub) to read as follows: Disclosure Of Conflicts (Core) - Conflicts must be disclosed to the Spark Foundation before the voting window (see Root Edit Token Holder Vote ) for the proposal begins. Abstaining For Non-Disclosed Conflicts (Core) - Abstaining for any reason other than a disclosed conflict is treated as non-performance under Delegate Offboarding . Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.4.2.2 - Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (Portal) / Spark - Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (GitHub) to read as follows: Conflict-of-Interest Disclosure (Core) - At onboarding, prospective Delegates must provide any known conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation. Disclosures must be updated as new conflicts arise. Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.8 - Registry of Delegates (Portal) / Spark - Registry of Delegates (GitHub) to read as follows: Registry of Delegates (Core) - The subdocuments herein list each active Delegate’s name, wallet address, effective date, and status. Entries are maintained via an Active Data document updated by the Operational Facilitator. Replace A.AG1.3.1.3.8.1 - Template Information For Each Delegate (Portal) / Spark - Template Information For Each Delegate (GitHub) to read as follows: Template Information For Each Delegate (Core) - The list of Delegates must follow this template for each recorded Delegate: [Insert Delegate Handle] Delegate Name: [Insert Handle] Delegate Wallet Address: Effective Date: Status: Active/Inactive/Suspended Add pyUSD To Risk Framework Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.6.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for Cash Stablecoins, a 0% Instance Financial RRC will be applied to Cash Stablecoins. In the near term, only USDS, sUSDS, Dai, sDai, USDC, USDT, and pyUSD (either held directly or through decentralized exchanges such as Curve) will be eligible for investment under this provision. Add a new subdocument of A.3.4.2.1 - Definitions (Portal) / A.3.4 - Definitions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.4.2.1.2 - Low Risk Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.4 - Low Risk Real World Assets (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Cash Stablecoins (Core) - Cash Stablecoins are defined as USDC, USDT, and pyUSD. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.4.2.2.1 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements. A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC in the LitePSM; USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; Cash Stablecoins in Curve (paired with USDS); USDC in GUNI 0.01%; and USDC in GUNI 0.05%. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral consists of Cash Stablecoins that do not qualify as Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral but can be converted to Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may include Cash Stablecoins deposited into lending protocols, Cash Stablecoins used to provide liquidity to decentralized exchanges, or liquid staking derivatives of cash stablecoins. Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral: The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles; The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: Cash Stablecoins in Curve (not paired with USDS); Cash Stablecoins in Uniswap; Cash Stablecoins in SparkLend; Cash Stablecoins in Aave; Cash Stablecoins in Morpho; and Cash Stablecoins in a Prime ALM Proxy. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may impose limitations on the size of exposures to these protocols or to specific pools within these protocols that qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral in order to prevent excessive risk to Sky. A.3.4 - Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Clarify Approval Requirements For Agent Root Edits Replace A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Spark - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Spark Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. Token holders may vote directly or through Delegates. See Delegation Framework . The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. Delete A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.2.1 - Circulating Supply Definition (Portal) / Spark - Circulating Supply Definition (GitHub) . Replace A.AG2.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Grove - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Grove Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. Replace A.AG3.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Launch Agent 2 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Launch Agent 2 Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. Replace A.AG4.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1.4 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Portal) / Launch Agent 3 - Root Edit Token Holder Vote (GitHub) to read as follows: Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Launch Agent 3 Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have more than 50% of votes cast, excluding abstentions, in favor to be approved. Move Authority For Approving Additional Lending Markets To The Core Executor Agents Replace A.3.3.2.1.1.1.1.2 - Covered Protocols (Portal) / A.3.3 - Covered Protocols (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Covered Protocols (Core) - The calculation of Instance Financial RRC for lending markets is applicable to the following protocols: Aave v2 Aave v3 SparkLend Morpho Maple The application by a Prime Agent of the Risk Framework for lending markets to any protocols not listed above must be approved by the Core Executor Agents. The Core Executor Agents shall consult with the Stability Scope Advisors and the Stability Facilitators in making this determination. Any such approval must be posted to the Sky Forum under the category for the Prime Agent. Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process Replace A.1.9.3.1.1.2 - SparkLend Multisig Number Of Signers (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Number Of Signers (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Number Of Signers (Core) - The SparkLend Security Access Multisig currently has a 3/5 signing requirement. Replace A.1.9.3.1.1.3 - SparkLend Multisig Current Signers (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Current Signers (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Current Signers (Core) - The SparkLend Security Access Multisig currently has the following signers: VoteWizard LDR Hexonaut MonetSupply LucasManuel Replace A.1.9.3.1.1.4 - SparkLend Multisig Signer Modifications (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Signer Modifications (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Culture And Research - SparkLend Multisig Signer Modifications (Core) - Modification of the signers of the SparkLend Security Access Multisig must be approved through a Governance Poll; no Executive Vote is required. The only exceptions to this are if: 1) a signer self-reports a loss of access to their private key due to any reason; or 2) a signer explicitly expresses their wish to be removed as a signer. Correct Responsible Party For Updating Active Data Replace A.2.3.8.1.2.3.6.4.1.1 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (Portal) / A.2.4 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Onboarding Integrators Active Data Update (Core) - A.2.4 - List Of Onboarding Integrators is updated as follows: Updated fields Onboarding Integrators New value: Delete the Integrator. Responsible Party: Operational GovOps Triggers: None Replace A.2.3.8.2.2.3.6.4.1.2 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (Portal) / A.2.4 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Current Integrators Active Data Update (Core) - A.2.4 - List Of Current Integrators is updated as follows: Updated fields Current Integrators New value: set to the name of the Integrator from the approved Proposal Reward Code New value: set to the Reward Code from the approved Proposal Tracking Methodology New value: set to the tracking methodology from the approved Proposal Responsible Party: Operational GovOps Triggers: None Complete Renaming Of “Star” To “Prime” Update the term Stars with Primes as specified in the linked Pull Request: Forthcoming Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal by aa-lex · Pull Request #50 · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub

firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Replace Date Of Finalization Of Risk Framework With Fixed Date - Replaces the date of finalization of the Risk Framework with a specific date of July 1, 2025 for certain milestones related to Spark and Grove TGE and income generation. Update Contract Naming And References To GSM Pause Delay - Updates the naming convention of the contracts in the Governance Security Article to be consistent with the Chainlog keys and standardizes references to the GSM Pause Delay. Add Definition Of Chainlog - Adds a definition of the Chainlog to the Atlas. Update Usage Of Tags Versus Categories - Clarifies that Star Agents should use their specified category when posting on the Sky Forum. Add Interim Logic For Launch Agent 2 And 3 In Root Edit Primitive - Adds interim logic for the way in which Launch Agent 2 and Launch Agent 3 can update their respective Artifacts. Clarify Destination Of Leftover AD Budget - Clarifies that any leftover funds in a derecognized AD’s Buffer, after deduction of penalties, should be paid out to the AD. Replace Date Of Finalization Of Risk Framework With Fixed Date Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.1 - Token Launch Penalty (Portal) / A.2.10 - Token Launch Penalty (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Token Launch Penalty (Core) - If either Spark or Grove (each, a “Star”) does not complete its Star Token Generation Event (“TGE”) by July 1, 2025, a penalty of thirty percent (30%) will apply. This penalty will be calculated on the income (as defined in A.2.10 - Income Definition ) the Star is receiving or is meant to receive (including revenue that has accrued but has not been transferred) until the TGE occurs. The penalty shall be deducted from the Genesis Capital Allocation at the time of the Capital Transfer. Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.4 - Treatment of Expenses Paid By Sky Pre-TGE (Portal) / A.2.10 - Treatment of Expenses Paid By Sky Pre-TGE (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Treatment of Expenses Paid By Sky Pre-TGE (Core) - Any operational or other expenses incurred by a Star and paid directly by Sky after July 1, 2025 shall be treated as an advance against the Star’s Genesis Capital Allocation. The total amount of such expenses shall be documented and shall be deducted from the Star’s allocated capital funds at the time of the Capital Transfer (as outlined in A.2.10 - Transfer Of Capital Funds ). Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.5 - Income Generation And Pre-TGE Credit (Portal) / A.2.10 - Income Generation And Pre-TGE Credit (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Income Generation And Pre-TGE Credit (Core) - “Income Generation” shall be deemed to commence on July 1, 2025. From that date until the Star’s TGE, seventy percent (70%) of any income generated by the Star’s activities shall be credited to its capital account (net of any expenses paid by Sky as per A.2.10 - Treatment of Expenses Paid By Sky Pre-TGE ), subject to any penalties. Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.6 - Income Definition (Portal) / A.2.10 - Income Definition (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Income Definition (Core) - “Income” means all revenues or fees received or accrued by the applicable Star after July 1, 2025, including: (i) Accessibility Rewards (see A.2.10 - Accessibility Reward Rate ), (ii) Accessibility Reward Bonus for 2025 (see A.2.10 - 2025 Bonus ), (iii) any Platform Fees charged to users, and (iv) Real World Asset fees charged to users, including any origination, servicing, or related charges, and (v) the blended cost of allocation spread between Junior and Senior Risk Capital. Update Contract Naming And References To GSM Pause Delay Replace A.1.9.2.2.3 - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception (Core) - The LINE_MOM contract manages the breaker for the Debt Ceilings of a configurable subset of the vault types in the Sky Protocol. This Debt Ceiling Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to reduce the debt ceilings of a pre-configured whitelist of vault types to zero without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay to expire. The Debt Ceiling Breaker affects both the Debt Ceiling and the Maximum Debt Ceiling of a given vault type when activated, disabling the Dynamic Debt Ceiling functionality for that vault type if enabled. To reverse the effect, parameters of affected vault types must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay. The whitelist may be configured via a successful governance proposal, but must wait for the GSM Pause Delay before changes come into effect. The whitelist is defined in A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception Whitelist and can be changed via the Weekly Governance Cycle. Replace A.1.9.2.2.6 - Dynamic Debt Ceiling Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Dynamic Debt Ceiling Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Dynamic Debt Ceiling Exception (Core) - The MCD_IAM_AUTO_LINE contract manages the debt ceiling parameters for many of Sky’s vault types according to preset rules. Keepers can use the contract to attempt to maintain a Target Available Debt in a given vault type. The contract modifies the debt ceiling up or down to maintain a level of available debt. This functionality is exceptional so that the Sky protocol can react to changes in debt demand more quickly than waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is a theoretical griefing attack on the IAM that prevents debt from being accessible in affected vault types. Replace A.1.9.2.2.7 - SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception (Core) - The SparkLend FREEZER_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay to either freeze or pause any markets in SparkLend. The contract also allows the undoing of such actions for any market in SparkLend. This functionality allows Sky Governance to react faster in an emergency. Freezing markets does not allow for new supplies or borrows, while pause restricts all market functionality, including deposits/withdrawals/borrows/repays and liquidations. Replace A.1.9.2.2.8 - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception (Core) - The SPLITTER_MOM contract allows for the disabling of the Smart Burn Engine without the GSM Pause Delay. This functionality is available so that Sky Governance can react to emergencies regarding the Smart Burn Engine. Since the Splitter contract also allocates USDS from the Surplus Buffer to USDS Staking Rewards, the activation of SPLITTER_MOM also disables these rewards until the activation is reversed by Sky Governance. Replace A.1.9.2.2.9 - PSM Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - PSM Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - PSM Breaker Exception (Core) - The LITE_PSM_MOM contract manages the breaker for swaps through the LitePSM. The PSM Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to halt swaps through the LitePSM. Replace A.1.9.2.2.10.2 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Bounded External Access Modules - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (Core) - The Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM) MCD_SPBEAM contract manages the rates applied to Sky Protocol’s native vaults as well as the savings rates. Whitelisted operators can use the SP-BEAM to modify rates without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The SP-BEAM modifies rates up or down within specified parameters. See A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module . This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to react to changes in market rates more quickly than waiting for the Governance and Spell Process execution and the GSM Pause Delay. The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting rates to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the SP-BEAM parameters and the SPBEAM_MOM. Replace A.1.9.2.2.11 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Core) - The SPBEAM_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the SP-BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the SPBEAM_MOM is activated, the SP-BEAM will not be able to change any rates in the system. If the SPBEAM_MOM has been triggered, it will still be possible to modify rates through the usual Executive Vote process, subject to the GSM Pause Delay. It serves as the single source of truth for contract addresses in the protocol. The Chainlog is available at https://chainlog.sky.money/ . lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Change Funding Source For Accessibility Reward Wallet - Updates the Accessibility Reward wallet to be funded by Executive Votes rather than the Launch Project. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates - Allows Spark delegates to disclose conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation instead of publicly to avoid compromising anonymity. Add pyUSD To Risk Framework - Adds rules for RRC and ASC for investments in pyUSD to the Risk Framework. Clarify Approval Requirements For Agent Root Edits - Makes minor edits to clarify approval threshold for Agent Root Edits and handling of abstentions. Move Authority For Approving Additional Lending Markets To The Core Executor Agents - Moves the authority for approving additional lending markets to the Core Executor Agents. Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process - Updates the SparkLend multisig and clarifies the governance process for updates to multisig signers. Correct Responsible Party For Updating Active Data - Corrects the Responsible Party for updating some Active Data to be Operational GovOps rather than the Operational Facilitator. Complete Renaming Of “Star” To “Prime” - Replaces remaining references in the Atlas to “Star” with “Prime”. The balance of this wallet may be topped up to 3 million USDS. This funding is subject to an Executive Vote. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.4.2.2.1 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements. A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC in the LitePSM; USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; Cash Stablecoins in Curve (paired with USDS); USDC in GUNI 0.01%; and USDC in GUNI 0.05%. Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral: The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles; The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels. firstSeen.title: Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal 2025-07-21
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Replace Date Of Finalization Of Risk Framework With Fixed Date - Replaces the date of finalization of the Risk Framework with a specific date of July 1, 2025 for certain milestones related to Spark and Grove TGE and income generation. Update Contract Naming And References To GSM Pause Delay - Updates the naming convention of the contracts in the Governance Security Article to be consistent with the Chainlog keys and standardizes references to the GSM Pause Delay. Add Definition Of Chainlog - Adds a definition of the Chainlog to the Atlas. Update Usage Of Tags Versus Categories - Clarifies that Star Agents should use their specified category when posting on the Sky Forum. Add Interim Logic For Launch Agent 2 And 3 In Root Edit Primitive - Adds interim logic for the way in which Launch Agent 2 and Launch Agent 3 can update their respective Artifacts. Clarify Destination Of Leftover AD Budget - Clarifies that any leftover funds in a derecognized AD’s Buffer, after deduction of penalties, should be paid out to the AD. Replace Date Of Finalization Of Risk Framework With Fixed Date Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.1 - Token Launch Penalty (Portal) / A.2.10 - Token Launch Penalty (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Token Launch Penalty (Core) - If either Spark or Grove (each, a “Star”) does not complete its Star Token Generation Event (“TGE”) by July 1, 2025, a penalty of thirty percent (30%) will apply. This penalty will be calculated on the income (as defined in A.2.10 - Income Definition ) the Star is receiving or is meant to receive (including revenue that has accrued but has not been transferred) until the TGE occurs. The penalty shall be deducted from the Genesis Capital Allocation at the time of the Capital Transfer. Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.4 - Treatment of Expenses Paid By Sky Pre-TGE (Portal) / A.2.10 - Treatment of Expenses Paid By Sky Pre-TGE (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Treatment of Expenses Paid By Sky Pre-TGE (Core) - Any operational or other expenses incurred by a Star and paid directly by Sky after July 1, 2025 shall be treated as an advance against the Star’s Genesis Capital Allocation. The total amount of such expenses shall be documented and shall be deducted from the Star’s allocated capital funds at the time of the Capital Transfer (as outlined in A.2.10 - Transfer Of Capital Funds ). Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.5 - Income Generation And Pre-TGE Credit (Portal) / A.2.10 - Income Generation And Pre-TGE Credit (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Income Generation And Pre-TGE Credit (Core) - “Income Generation” shall be deemed to commence on July 1, 2025. From that date until the Star’s TGE, seventy percent (70%) of any income generated by the Star’s activities shall be credited to its capital account (net of any expenses paid by Sky as per A.2.10 - Treatment of Expenses Paid By Sky Pre-TGE ), subject to any penalties. Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.6 - Income Definition (Portal) / A.2.10 - Income Definition (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Income Definition (Core) - “Income” means all revenues or fees received or accrued by the applicable Star after July 1, 2025, including: (i) Accessibility Rewards (see A.2.10 - Accessibility Reward Rate ), (ii) Accessibility Reward Bonus for 2025 (see A.2.10 - 2025 Bonus ), (iii) any Platform Fees charged to users, and (iv) Real World Asset fees charged to users, including any origination, servicing, or related charges, and (v) the blended cost of allocation spread between Junior and Senior Risk Capital. Update Contract Naming And References To GSM Pause Delay Replace A.1.9.2.2.3 - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception (Core) - The LINE_MOM contract manages the breaker for the Debt Ceilings of a configurable subset of the vault types in the Sky Protocol. This Debt Ceiling Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to reduce the debt ceilings of a pre-configured whitelist of vault types to zero without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay to expire. The Debt Ceiling Breaker affects both the Debt Ceiling and the Maximum Debt Ceiling of a given vault type when activated, disabling the Dynamic Debt Ceiling functionality for that vault type if enabled. To reverse the effect, parameters of affected vault types must be reconfigured with an Executive Vote which is subject to the GSM Pause Delay. The whitelist may be configured via a successful governance proposal, but must wait for the GSM Pause Delay before changes come into effect. The whitelist is defined in A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Debt Ceiling Breaker Exception Whitelist and can be changed via the Weekly Governance Cycle. Replace A.1.9.2.2.6 - Dynamic Debt Ceiling Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Dynamic Debt Ceiling Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Dynamic Debt Ceiling Exception (Core) - The MCD_IAM_AUTO_LINE contract manages the debt ceiling parameters for many of Sky’s vault types according to preset rules. Keepers can use the contract to attempt to maintain a Target Available Debt in a given vault type. The contract modifies the debt ceiling up or down to maintain a level of available debt. This functionality is exceptional so that the Sky protocol can react to changes in debt demand more quickly than waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The risk opened up by this exceptional functionality is a theoretical griefing attack on the IAM that prevents debt from being accessible in affected vault types. Replace A.1.9.2.2.7 - SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - SparkLend Freezer Mom Exception (Core) - The SparkLend FREEZER_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay to either freeze or pause any markets in SparkLend. The contract also allows the undoing of such actions for any market in SparkLend. This functionality allows Sky Governance to react faster in an emergency. Freezing markets does not allow for new supplies or borrows, while pause restricts all market functionality, including deposits/withdrawals/borrows/repays and liquidations. Replace A.1.9.2.2.8 - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Smart Burn Engine Breaker Exception (Core) - The SPLITTER_MOM contract allows for the disabling of the Smart Burn Engine without the GSM Pause Delay. This functionality is available so that Sky Governance can react to emergencies regarding the Smart Burn Engine. Since the Splitter contract also allocates USDS from the Surplus Buffer to USDS Staking Rewards, the activation of SPLITTER_MOM also disables these rewards until the activation is reversed by Sky Governance. Replace A.1.9.2.2.9 - PSM Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - PSM Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - PSM Breaker Exception (Core) - The LITE_PSM_MOM contract manages the breaker for swaps through the LitePSM. The PSM Breaker allows a successful governance proposal to halt swaps through the LitePSM. Replace A.1.9.2.2.10.2 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Bounded External Access Modules - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Exception (Core) - The Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module (SP-BEAM) MCD_SPBEAM contract manages the rates applied to Sky Protocol’s native vaults as well as the savings rates. Whitelisted operators can use the SP-BEAM to modify rates without waiting for the GSM Pause Delay. The SP-BEAM modifies rates up or down within specified parameters. See A.3.9 - Measures For Endgame Transition - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module . This functionality allows the Sky Protocol to react to changes in market rates more quickly than waiting for the Governance and Spell Process execution and the GSM Pause Delay. The risk opened up by this functionality is malicious action by whitelisted operators setting rates to undesirable values. This risk can be mitigated through the SP-BEAM parameters and the SPBEAM_MOM. Replace A.1.9.2.2.11 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Core) - The SPBEAM_MOM contract allows Sky Governance to bypass the GSM Pause Delay and disable the Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module. This functionality allows Sky Governance to react more quickly in an emergency, e.g., if an operator of the SP-BEAM is hacked or is a malicious actor. Once the SPBEAM_MOM is activated, the SP-BEAM will not be able to change any rates in the system. If the SPBEAM_MOM has been triggered, it will still be possible to modify rates through the usual Executive Vote process, subject to the GSM Pause Delay. Add Definition Of Chainlog Add a new subdocument of A.1.9.1 - General Provisions (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - General Provisions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.1.9.1.1 - Spell Team Anonymity (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - General Provisions - Spell Team Anonymity (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - General Provisions - Chainlog (Core) - The Chainlog is an on-chain, governance-managed registry that records the official addresses of Sky’s core smart contracts. Each contract entry in the Chainlog is identified by a unique key (“Chainlog key”), which is used to reference the contract in documentation, governance actions, and integrations. lastEdit.title: 2025-08-25 Atlas Weekly Cycle Proposal Edits
lastEdit.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Change Funding Source For Accessibility Reward Wallet - Updates the Accessibility Reward wallet to be funded by Executive Votes rather than the Launch Project. Protect Anonymity Of Spark Delegates - Allows Spark delegates to disclose conflicts of interest to the Spark Foundation instead of publicly to avoid compromising anonymity. Add pyUSD To Risk Framework - Adds rules for RRC and ASC for investments in pyUSD to the Risk Framework. Clarify Approval Requirements For Agent Root Edits - Makes minor edits to clarify approval threshold for Agent Root Edits and handling of abstentions. Move Authority For Approving Additional Lending Markets To The Core Executor Agents - Moves the authority for approving additional lending markets to the Core Executor Agents. Update SparkLend Multisig And Clarify Update Process - Updates the SparkLend multisig and clarifies the governance process for updates to multisig signers. Correct Responsible Party For Updating Active Data - Corrects the Responsible Party for updating some Active Data to be Operational GovOps rather than the Operational Facilitator. Complete Renaming Of “Star” To “Prime” - Replaces remaining references in the Atlas to “Star” with “Prime”. The Accessibility Facilitators then pay the Accessibility Reward from the Accessibility Reward Controller Wallet located on the Ethereum Mainnet at 0x05f471262d15eeca4059dade070e5bed509a4e73 within seven (7) days of the end of every month. The balance of this wallet may be topped up to 3 million USDS. This funding is subject to an Executive Vote. Abstaining For Non-Disclosed Conflicts (Core) - Abstaining for any reason other than a disclosed conflict is treated as non-performance under Delegate Offboarding . Disclosures must be updated as new conflicts arise. Entries are maintained via an Active Data document updated by the Operational Facilitator. In the near term, only USDS, sUSDS, Dai, sDai, USDC, USDT, and pyUSD (either held directly or through decentralized exchanges such as Curve) will be eligible for investment under this provision. Add a new subdocument of A.3.4.2.1 - Definitions (Portal) / A.3.4 - Definitions (GitHub) . This document should be located directly after A.3.4.2.1.2 - Low Risk Real World Assets (Portal) / A.3.4 - Low Risk Real World Assets (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Cash Stablecoins (Core) - Cash Stablecoins are defined as USDC, USDT, and pyUSD. Replace the subdocuments of A.3.4.2.2.1 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements. A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC in the LitePSM; USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; Cash Stablecoins in Curve (paired with USDS); USDC in GUNI 0.01%; and USDC in GUNI 0.05%. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral consists of Cash Stablecoins that do not qualify as Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral but can be converted to Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may include Cash Stablecoins deposited into lending protocols, Cash Stablecoins used to provide liquidity to decentralized exchanges, or liquid staking derivatives of cash stablecoins. Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral: The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles; The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: Cash Stablecoins in Curve (not paired with USDS); Cash Stablecoins in Uniswap; Cash Stablecoins in SparkLend; Cash Stablecoins in Aave; Cash Stablecoins in Morpho; and Cash Stablecoins in a Prime ALM Proxy. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may impose limitations on the size of exposures to these protocols or to specific pools within these protocols that qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral in order to prevent excessive risk to Sky. A.3.4 - Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral. A.3.3 - Definition (Core) - Legal Recourse Assets (”LRAs”) are Real World Assets where legal recourse can be used to recover the assets even if the smart contract is technically hacked or exploited. A.3.3 - Exposure Calculation (Core) - The exposure for investments in Legal Recourse Assets is calculated according to the following formula: Exposure = Equivalent Loss * Effective Age + Raw Exposure * (1 - Effective Age) The parameters of this formula are defined in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Equivalent Loss (Core) - Equivalent Loss is an estimate of the loss that the holder of a Legal Recourse Asset would experience if they had to use legal recourse to recover the assets, based on a combination of expected time to recovery and litigation financing costs. The value of the Expected Frozen Duration is 0.5. A.3.3 - Litigation Financing Costs (Core) - Litigation Financing Costs are the annual costs of borrowing against the right to receive the future recovery of the assets underlying the Legal Recourse Asset through legal recourse. The value of the Litigation Financing Costs is 20%. A.3.3 - Effective Age (Core) - The Effective Age is calculated as specified in A.3.3 - Effective Age except that the Effective Age cannot exceed one (1) year. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of “eligible assets” for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See A.3.3 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC) . For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Star, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components. Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Star Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Star Agent’s TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Star Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations. Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Star Agent’s compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)). firstSeen.title: 2025-05-26 Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the following proposal to prepare for the launch of the SPK token. This proposal contains the following edits: Build Out Allocation System Primitive - Builds out the Allocation System Primitive, including the process for Star Agents to comply with the risk framework. Add Spark - Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Spark and Launch Agent 1. Add Sky - Spark / Launch Agent 1 Ecosystem Accord - Adds an Ecosystem Accord between Sky, Spark, and Launch Agent 1. Add Logic Regarding Key Interest Rates - Adds logic regarding how the Base Rate is set and how it relates to the Agent Credit Line Borrow Rate. Update Risk Framework - Updates the risk framework to include a new model for lending markets and models for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk. Rename First Loss Capital To Junior Risk Capital - Renames First Loss Capital to Junior Risk Capital to better align with other terminology in the Atlas. Update Logic Regarding Distribution Of Agent Tokens - Clarifies the distribution of Agent Tokens received by Sky under an Ecosystem Accord. Update Spark Liquidity Layer Documentation - Updates the documentation of the Spark Liquidity Layer to reflect that it is an implementation of the Allocation System Primitive. Update Spark Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates Spark Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Spark. Update Launch Agent 1 Artifact Based On Ecosystem Accords - Updates the Launch Agent 1 Artifact to reflect the Ecosystem Accords entered into by Launch Agent 1. Given the size of the proposal, we are following the same approach that we used for the Agent Launch. First, we have published the proposal to a public Notion page: [Public] Atlas Edit Weekly Proposal For SPK Launch . Second, we have generated an HTML version of the Proposal; this allows us to guarantee that the Proposal submitted herein is immutable - it cannot be altered. We have attached the HTML file to the Notion page linked above. Simply click on the file, and your browser will download it. Please note: due to a Notion bug, internal references in the Proposal are not displayed correctly in the HTML file. To see the internal references and get the best experience, we would recommend that community members review the Notion page. Using the process below, community members can independently verify the contents of the Proposal submitted herein: Download the HTML file from the Notion page Open it in an editor such as VS Code Copy the contents into the hash generator at Keccak-256 - Online Tools Verify that the hash is equal to bedf45dceb0748041815e6a534eba006a83d00aded64c96b0d2ee7ac297f199d

firstSeen.title: Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal 2025-08-04
firstSeen.summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Document Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation - Documents the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation that will be used in Stage 1 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. Update Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirements - Updates the minimum level of Actively Stabilizing Collateral that Stars must maintain and defines Resting versus Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Update Required Risk Capital For Real World Assets - Updates the Required Risk Capital for Real World Assets to take into account new versus existing deployments. Remove Exceptions For Maple In Risk Framework - Removes exceptions for Maple from the Risk Framework since risk assessments for Maple have now been completed. Update Spark / Grove Ecosystem Accord To Include Ethena Revenue Share - Adds the terms for sharing revenue from investments in USDe and sUSDe to the Ecosystem Accord between Spark and Grove. Rename yUSDS to stUSDS - Updates the name of yUSDS to stUSDS. Incorporate Linear Interpolation Module - Incorporates the Linear Interpolation Module and its features in the Atlas. Document Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation Replace A.2.5.1.2.1.1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.2.6 - Stage 1 Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (Core) - In Stage 1 of the implementation of the Monthly Settlement Cycle, the net amount due from each Star to Sky will be calculated using a Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation as specified in the documents herein. A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Demand Side Primitives And Agent Rate (Core) - The amount due from Sky to each Star with respect to Demand Side Primitives and the Agent Rate is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Accessibility Reward (Core) - The amount due from Sky to a Star in a month with respect to the Accessibility Reward is the amount earned by the Star with respect to all USDS and sUSDS balances marked with the Star’s reward codes. See A.2.4 - Accessibility Reward Primitive . This includes any Bonus Accessibility Reward. See A.2.10 - 2025 Bonus . A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Agent Rate (Core) - The amount due from Sky to a Star in a month with respect to the Agent Rate is calculated as specified in A.3.2 - Core Stability Parameters - Parameters - Agent Rate . A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Accessibility Reward And Agent Rate (Core) - The amount due from Sky to a Star in a month with respect to the Accessibility Reward and the Agent Rate is the sum of the amounts specified in A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Accessibility Reward and A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Agent Rate. A.2.6 - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives (Core) - The amount due from each Star to Sky with respect to Supply Side Primitives is calculated as specified in the documents herein. A.2.6 - Step 1: Calculate Total Allocation System Revenue (Core) - First, Total Allocation System Revenue is calculated for each Star for the month. Total Allocation System Revenue for a Star in a month is the sum of Instance Revenue for each Active Instance of the Allocation System Primitive that the Star has deployed. A.2.6 - Instance Revenue (Core) - Instance Revenue for an Allocation System Instance for a month is all earnings from that Instance. A.2.6 - Step 2: Calculate Total Allocation System Profit (Core) - Second, Total Allocation System Profit is calculated for each Star for the month. Total Allocation System Profit for a Star in a month is the sum of Instance Profit for each Active Instance of the Allocation System Primitive that the Star has deployed. A.2.6 - Instance Profit (Core) - Instance Profit for an Allocation System Instance is equal to the greater of (1) Instance Revenue (see A.2.6 - Instance Revenue) minus Instance Expenses (see A.2.6 - Instance Expense) and (2) zero. A.2.6 - Instance Expense (Core) - Instance Expense for an Allocation System Instance for a month is the interest expense on the funds from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio invested in the Instance. It is calculated on a per block basis based on the amount invested from Sky’s Collateral Portfolio and the Base Rate. A.2.6 - Step 3: Calculate Adjusted Allocation System Profit (Core) - Third, Adjusted Allocation System Profit is calculated for each Star for the month. Adjusted Allocation System Profit for a Star in a month is Total Allocation System Profit minus the Distortion Penalty (see A.2.6 - Distortion Penalty) and the Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty (see A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty). A.2.6 - Distortion Penalty (Core) - The Distortion Penalty is a discretionary penalty designed to mitigate the potential misalignment caused by the asymmetric nature of the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation, where Stars earn profits on Allocation System Instances that earn more than the Base Rate but do not suffer losses when Instances earn less than the Base Rate. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may assess a penalty of up to 100% of Total Allocation System Profit (see A.2.6 - Step 2: Calculate Total Allocation System Profit) if it determines that a Star’s decisions were distorted by this incentive structure. A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty (Core) - The Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Penalty is a formulaic penalty designed to prevent Stars from holding excessive amounts of low yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral. The penalty, as a percentage of the Total Allocation System Profit, is the lesser of (1) ten times the Excess Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Percentage and (2) 100%. A.2.6 - Excess Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Percentage (Core) - The Excess Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral Percentage for a Star is equal to the excess of (1) its Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (see A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral) as a percentage of its Collateral Portfolio above (2) its Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral (see A.3.4 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral ) as a percentage of its Collateral Portfolio. A.2.6 - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Low Yield Actively Stabilizing Collateral is Actively Stabilizing Collateral (see A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral ) that earns less than the Base Rate. A.2.6 - Step 4: Calculate Amount Due To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives (Core) - Fourth, the amount due to Sky with respect to Supply Side Primitives is calculated for each Star for the month. The amount due to Sky with respect to Supply Side Primitives is Total Allocation System Revenue (see A.2.6 - Step 1: Calculate Total Allocation System Revenue) minus Adjusted Allocation System Profit (see A.2.6 - Step 3: Calculate Adjusted Allocation System Profit). A.2.6 - Net Amount Due From Stars To Sky (Core) - The net amount due from each Star to Sky is the amount due from the Star to Sky with respect to Supply Side Primitives (see A.2.6 - Amount Due From Stars To Sky With Respect To Supply Side Primitives) plus any amount due from the Star to Sky with respect to the Token Launch Penalty (see A.2.10 - Token Launch Penalty ) minus the amount due from Sky to the Star with respect to Demand Side Primitives and the Agent Rate (see A.2.6 - Amount Due From Sky To Stars With Respect To Demand Side Primitives And Agent Rate). Net amounts due from a Star to Sky are transferred from the Star’s Treasury to the Surplus Buffer through a Star Spell included in an Executive Vote. Net amounts due from Sky to a Star are transferred from the Surplus Buffer to the Star’s Treasury through an Executive Vote. Delete A.2.5.1.2.1.3.2 - Documentation Of Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (Portal) / A.2.6 - Sky Core Monthly Settlement Cycle - Monthly Settlement Cycle Overview - Implementation - Stage 1 - Stage 1 Actions - Documentation Of Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation (GitHub) . Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.8.1 - Token Launch Penalty (Portal) / A.2.10 - Token Launch Penalty (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Token Launch Penalty (Core) - If either Spark or Grove (each, a “Star”) does not complete its Star Token Generation Event (“TGE”) by July 1, 2025, a penalty of thirty percent (30%) will apply. This penalty will be calculated on the income (as defined in A.2.10 - Income Definition) the Star is receiving or is meant to receive (including revenue that has accrued but has not been transferred) until the TGE occurs. The penalty shall be deducted from the Genesis Capital Allocation at the time of the Capital Transfer. If the Star has already received its Genesis Capital Allocation, then the 30% penalty is paid as part of the Monthly Settlement Cycle. See A.2.6 - Net Amount Due From Stars To Sky. Update Actively Stabilizing Collateral Requirements Replace A.3.4.2.2 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.3.4 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.4 - Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Star Agents must maintain at least 25% of their Collateral Portfolio in Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Replace A.3.4.2.2.1 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Portal) / A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (GitHub) and its subdocuments to read as follows: A.3.4 - Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Actively Stabilizing Collateral is the sum of (1) Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral and (2) Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral. A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread). Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral includes cash stablecoins (e.g., USDC, USDT) in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements. A.3.4 - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC in the LitePSM; USDC in the PSM3 on Base, Arbitrum, Unichain, Optimism; USDT in Curve; USDC in GUNI 0.01%; and USDC in GUNI 0.05%. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral consists of cash stablecoins that do not qualify as Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral but can be converted to Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may include cash stablecoins deposited into lending protocols, cash stablecoins used to provide liquidity to decentralized exchanges, or liquid staking derivatives of cash stablecoins. Assets must satisfy the following requirements to qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral: The assets must be verifiable onchain or through reputable APIs or oracles; The assets must be able to be converted into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral within 15 minutes under normal market conditions; and The process to convert the assets into Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral must be fully automated and triggered automatically when ASC falls below specified levels. A.3.4 - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral Calculations (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral is currently calculated as the sum of: USDC and USDT in Curve; USDC and USDT in Uniswap; USDC and USDT in SparkLend; USDC and USDT in Aave; USDC and USDT in Morpho; and USDC USDT in a Star ALM Proxy. The Core Executor Agent, in consultation with the Stability Facilitators and the Stability Scope Advisors, may impose limitations on the size of exposures to these protocols or to specific pools within these protocols that qualify as Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral in order to prevent excessive risk to Sky. A.3.4 - Maximum Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral (Core) - Latent Actively Stabilizing Collateral may not exceed 25% of Actively Stabilizing Collateral. Update Required Risk Capital For Real World Assets Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.1.1.2 - Instance Total RRC (Portal) / A.3.3 - Instance Total RRC (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Application To Real World Assets (Core) - Investments in Real World Assets, as defined in A.3.3 - Real World Assets , have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Admin RRC as specified in the documents herein. An additional type of Legal RRC, reflecting the unique risks of these assets, will be incorporated in future iterations of the Risk Framework. A.3.3 - Short Term Application To Real World Assets (Core) - In the short term, investments in the following Real World Assets automatically have Instance Smart Contract RRC and Instance Admin RRC of zero: • BUIDL • JTRSY • USTB • JAAA through Centrifuge v2 All other investments in RWAs have Instance Total RRC of 100%. A.3.3 - Long Term Application To Real World Assets (Core) - In the long term, adapted frameworks for Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk for Real World Assets must be developed. These frameworks should take into account (1) the reduced risk in an expected worst case scenario due to the legal backstop on these assets and (2) the factors normally considered in assessing Smart Contract Risk and Administrative Risk. A.3.3 - Incorporation Of Additional Types Of RRC (Core) - Additional types of RRC reflecting other risk factors, including legal risk and oracle risk, will be incorporated in future iterations of the Risk Framework. A.3.3 - Inability To Calculate Types Of RRC (Core) - If Instance Financial RRC, Instance Smart Contract Risk RRC, or Instance Admin Risk RRC for an Instance cannot be calculated then the Instance Total RRC is 100%. Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3 - Financial Risk Models (Portal) / A.3.3 - Financial Risk Models (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Financial Risk Models (Core) - The conceptual framework for financial risk is implemented through asset class specific risk models. The documents herein define the asset classes that risk models exist or are being developed for, including the high level approach and examples of relevant assets. Replace A.3.3.1.1.3.3.2.4.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) and its subdocument to read as follows: A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (Core) - In the near term pending development of the implementation of the model for Real World Assets, the following Instance Financial RRC Ratios will apply: • BUIDL, JTRSY, and USTB - 0% Instance Financial RRC Ratio • JAAA on Ethereum Mainnet - 1.6% Instance Financial RRC Ratio • JAAA on Avalanche - 2.1% Instance Financial RRC Ratio In the near term, only BUIDL, JTRSY, USTB, and JAAA through Centrifuge v2 will be eligible for investment under this provision. All other investments in Real World Assets have a 100% Instance Total RRC as specified in A.3.3 - Short Term Application To Real World Assets. A.3.3 - Additional Restrictions On Investments In JAAA On Avalanche (Core) - Investments in JAAA on Avalanche are subject to the following additional restrictions: • The initial deployment of capital into JAAA on Avalanche may not exceed 20 million USDS; • Each additional deployment of capital into JAAA must be approved by the Stability Scope Advisors; • The Star must be below a 90% Risk Tolerance Ratio on a pro forma basis assuming that each additional deployment of capital into JAAA requires 100% Instance Total RRC; and • Total investments in JAAA on Avalanche may not exceed 250 million USDS. Remove Exceptions For Maple Delete A.3.3.2.1.2.4.1 - Maple (Portal) / A.3.3 - Maple (GitHub) Delete A.3.3.2.1.3.3.1 - Maple (Portal) / A.3.3 - Maple (GitHub) Update Spark / Grove Ecosystem Accord To Include Ethena Revenue Share Add new subdocuments of A.2.9.1.1.2 - Accord Substantive Terms (Portal) / A.2.10 - Accord Substantive Terms (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.2.9.1.1.2.8 - Grand Prix Airdrops (Portal) / A.2.10 - Grand Prix Airdrops (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - USDe and sUSDe Revenue Share (Core) - Spark and Grove agree to share revenue from USDe and sUSDe as specified in the subdocuments herein. A.2.10 - Revenue Share (Core) - Spark and Grove will share 50% of all revenue and expenses associated with Spark’s Allocation System investments in USDe and sUSDe. Revenue includes (1) protocol yield on the amount deployed into these assets, (2) any OTC or negotiated arrangements, payments, or incentives, and (3) manual payments or rebates related to withdrawal activity. Expenses include all costs associated with Spark’s investment in USDe and sUSDe, including mint / burn fees, swap fees, and costs of borrowing funds from Sky. A.2.10 - Risk Capital Share (Core) - Grove agrees to rent to Spark 50% of the Required Risk Capital associated with Spark’s investments in USDe and sUSDe as a Junior Risk Capital Rental. See A.2.4 - Junior Risk Capital Rental Primitive . A.2.10 - Implementation (Core) - Spark and Grove expressly intend that Grove shares in 50% of the risks of Spark’s investment in USDe and sUSDe and not in the risk of any other investments by Spark. To the extent that USDe or sUSDe investments experience losses and Spark is allocated a greater than 50% share of those losses relative to Grove under the TIP JRC mechanism (see A.3.3 - Initial Loss Absorption By “Tip JRC” ), Grove will transfer funds to Spark so that Grove and Spark each bear 50% of the losses that occur. To the extent that Spark experiences losses on investments other than USDe or sUSDe and a portion of those losses is allocated to the Junior Risk Capital rented from Grove, Spark shall reimburse Grove for those losses. A.2.10 - Term (Core) - This revenue share shall be effective retroactively, dated back to the launch of Spark’s allocation into USDe and sUSDe beginning the week of July 14, 2025. It shall remain in effect until one of the following conditions is met, whichever occurs first: Grove begins to allocate capital to USDe or sUSDe directly; or Spark or Grove terminates the revenue share, with reasonable advance notice to the other party. Any changes to the structure or scope of this arrangement will be discussed transparently and approved by both Spark and Grove. Rename yUSDS to stUSDS Update the term yUSDS with stUSDS as specified in the linked Pull Request: Forthcoming Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposal by aa-lex · Pull Request #37 · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub Incorporate Linear Interpolation Module Add new subdocuments of A.1.9.2.2 - Exceptions (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Exceptions (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly after A.1.9.2.2.11 - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (Portal) / A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Stability Parameter Bounded External Access Module Breaker Exception (GitHub) to read as follows: A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module (Core) - The Linear Interpolation Module ( lerp ) is a smart contract tool that allows a governance parameter to be adjusted on a straight-line basis over time, without requiring additional Executive Votes. The Linear Interpolation Module refers to the smart contract logic that enables time-based parameter changes. To deploy individual lerp instances, each of which manages the adjustment of a specific parameter over time, the Linear Interpolation Module Factory contract is used. Once authorized through an Executive Vote, the lerp may enact parameter changes without being subject to the GSM Pause Delay. The subdocuments herein specify the features of the lerp and its authorized use. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Features (Core) - The lerp must be activated in an Executive Vote but can thereafter change the value of the designated parameter without additional Executive Votes. Each lerp instance is defined in terms of a start value, representing the desired starting value, an end value, representing the desired ending value, and a duration over which the parameter will be adjusted between the starting value and the ending value. Any user can then permissionlessly call tick to set the governance parameter to the appropriate value based on the time elapsed. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Parameters (Core) - Each lerp instance has the following parameters: target - The target contract in which a parameter is being changed what - The name of the parameter being changed startTime - The starting time of this lerp instance start - The starting value of that parameter end - The ending value of that parameter duration - How long this lerp instance will run for done - Indicates whether this given lerp instance is completed or not A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Factory (Core) - lerp instances are created using a factory contract LERP_FAB that contains standard logic for creating those instances and maintains a registry of all active lerp instances. The contract may also be used to cancel an existing lerp instance through the remove function. The factory contract provides a list method that lists the addresses of all active lerp instances, as well as a tall (short for “tick all”) method that calls tick on all active contracts. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Usage Process Definition (Core) - The subdocuments herein define the governance process for using the Linear Interpolation Module. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Authorization (Core) - The Facilitators responsible for the Scope that governs the parameter to be adjusted by the Linear Interpolation Module, in consultation with the Scope Advisor(s), may recommend deploying the Linear Interpolation Module for parameter adjustments. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Linear Interpolation Module Consideration (Core) - The Facilitators must take into consideration the benefits and costs with using the Linear Interpolation Module. A longer duration has the benefit of adjusting the parameter more slowly, giving users more time to adjust. However, the drawback of a longer duration is that the parameter will not reach its desired end value for a longer period of time. When the cost of a parameter not being at its desired value is high, use of the Linear Interpolation Module is not appropriate and the parameter should be adjusted to its desired value following the required process. A.1.9 - Sky Core Governance Security - Governance Security Delay Requirements - Governance Process For Linear Interpolation Module (Core) - The process to utilize the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust a parameter must follow the same governance process required to modify the designated parameter. If the parameter can be updated directly through an Executive Vote, then utilizing the Linear Interpolation Module to adjust it may also be included directly in an Executive Vote. This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas. Core GovOps validates the Star Agent’s reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Star Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of “eligible assets” for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See A.3.3 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC) . For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Star, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components. Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Star Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Star Agent’s TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Star Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations. Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Star Agent’s compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)). These deployments will be subject to the approval of Operational GovOps. Correct Issues In The SPK Launch Proposal Replace A.2.3.9.1.1.2.2.1.3.2.1 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (Portal) / A.2.4 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.4 - Core GovOps TRC Report Validation Process (Core) -Core GovOps receives TRC Reports from Stars on a regular basis and must perform the following validation process. Core GovOps verifies against the Atlas any Ecosystem Accord referenced in the TRC Report for sourced Star-External Junior Risk Capital (SEJRC) or rented Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas. Core GovOps validates the Star Agent’s reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Star Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of “eligible assets” for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See A.3.3 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC) . For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Star, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components. Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Star Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Star Agent’s TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Star Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations. Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Star Agent’s compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)). Core GovOps verifies against the Atlas any Ecosystem Accord referenced in the TRC Report for sourced Star-External Junior Risk Capital (SEJRC) or rented Originated Senior Risk Capital (OSRC). This includes confirming the existence, current validity, and terms of such Accords as formally recorded within the Atlas. Core GovOps validates the Star Agent’s reported IJRC by reconciling the reported IJRC amount and its constituent asset composition against the actual on-chain state of the Star Agent’s designated SubProxy account. This involves direct on-chain verification of asset balances. Core GovOps verifies that all assets reported as IJRC and held within the SubProxy account meet the definition of “eligible assets” for IJRC as defined by the Atlas. See A.3.3 - Internal Junior Risk Capital (IJRC) . For reported Tokenized External Junior Risk Capital (TEJRC) and Originated Senior Risk Capital directly originated by the Star, Core GovOps validates the reported amounts and statuses by cross-referencing data from the relevant smart contract systems. This may involve querying TEJRC pool contracts, OSRC auction records, and other on-chain infrastructure to confirm the existence, ownership, and eligibility of these capital components. Core GovOps reviews all attestations and disclosures made by the Star Agent in the TRC Report. This review focuses on understanding the Star Agent’s TRC compliance with Aggregate RRC throughout the entire reporting period. This assessment is critical for identifying intra-period shortfalls that might not be visible to on-chain monitoring systems or reflected in the end-of-period snapshot alone. The assessment process may include requiring the Star Agent to provide supplementary documentation, verifiable evidence, or independent third-party confirmations for material off-chain claims or attestations concerning intra-period events; and/or cross-referencing disclosed off-chain information with relevant on-chain indicators or transactions that might corroborate or contradict the attestations. Finally, Core GovOps independently calculates and verifies the Star Agent’s compliance with all Atlas-defined capital sourcing ratios (e.g., External Per Internal (EPI), Senior Per Junior (SPJ)).
